definition_zh: 马车；车厢；运输
definition_en: a vehicle with wheels pulled by horses, or a separate section of a train
core_image: 一个带轮的车厢，被马或机车拉着往前走
scene: 马车沿着乡间小路慢慢走。 The carriage moved slowly along the country road.
sceneCN: 这里 carriage 是「马车」（第 1 个义项：由马拉的四轮载客车）；句意是马车沿着乡间小路慢慢走。

derivatives.zh: 与 carriage 同根，义为「携带、运送」
carry 加 -er 构成，义为「承运人、携带者」
carriage 与 way 复合，义为「车行道」

senses.title: A horse-drawn passenger vehicle
senses.definition: a wheeled vehicle pulled by horses and used for carrying passengers
senses.definitionCN: 由马拉动、用来载客的四轮车辆
senses.example: They hired a carriage for the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为婚礼租了一辆马车。
senses.why: Old French cariage meant the act of carrying, and the vehicle that carried people took the name.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 cariage 意为「运送」，用来载人的车便承接了这个名字。

senses.title: A separate section of a train
senses.definition: one of the separate parts of a train where passengers sit
senses.definitionCN: 列车中供乘客乘坐的一节独立部分
senses.example: We found seats in the last carriage.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在最后一节车厢找到了座位。
senses.why: A railway carriage is the same wheeled passenger box, now pulled by an engine.
senses.whyCN: 火车车厢就是同一个载人带轮盒子，只是改由机车牵引。

senses.title: The transport of goods
senses.definition: the business or cost of moving goods from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 把货物从一处运到另一处的业务或费用
senses.example: The contract covers the carriage of goods by sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这份合同涵盖海运货物运输。
senses.why: The oldest abstract sense is simply carrying, which survives in trade and legal language.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的抽象义就是「运送」，它保留在贸易与法律用语中。

intro.en: Carriage first meant the act of carrying, then the vehicle that does the carrying.
intro.cn: carriage 最初指「运送」这个动作，后来指执行运送的车辆。

items.en: carrus named a wagon, the root of the whole carrying family.
items.cn: carrus 指马车，是整组「运送」词汇的根。

items.en: carricare meant to load a cart with goods.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 carricare 意为「往车上装货」。

items.en: cariage named the act of transporting and the charge for it.
items.cn: 古法语 cariage 指运输行为及其费用。

items.en: English borrowed carriage for transport, then for the coach that carried people.
items.cn: 英语借入 carriage 指运输，随后指载人的马车。

items.en: Railways gave the word its sense of a passenger car, which remains in British English.
items.cn: 铁路赋予它「客车车厢」的义项，这一用法保留在英式英语中。

note.en: Carriage is the vehicle and the act, and it shares its root with carry and cargo.
note.cn: carriage 既是车辆也是行为，并与 carry、cargo 同根。

entries.definition: to hold something and take it somewhere
entries.definitionCN: 携带、运送，与 carriage 同根。

entries.definition: a person or company that transports goods
entries.definitionCN: 承运人、运输公司，由 carry 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: goods carried by ship or aircraft
entries.definitionCN: 船或飞机运载的货物，与 carriage 同出 carricare。

entries.definition: a strong four-wheeled vehicle for loads
entries.definitionCN: 结实的四轮载货车，与马车同类。

entries.definition: a comfortable bus or a horse-drawn passenger vehicle
entries.definitionCN: 舒适的长途客车，或旧时的载客马车。

entries.definition: a small vehicle pushed or pulled by hand or animal

normalIntro.en: Carriage is the noun of carrying: the act first, the vehicle second.
normalIntro.cn: carriage 是「运送」的名词：先有动作，后有车辆。

normal.en: carriage and carry share the same root, from Latin carricare, to load.
normal.cn: carriage 与 carry 同根，来自拉丁语 carricare（装车）。

normal.en: The -age ending often makes a noun of action, as in carriage and marriage.
normal.cn: -age 结尾常把动作变成名词，如 carriage、marriage。

normal.en: railway carriage is the British term for a passenger car.
normal.cn: railway carriage 是英式英语里「客车车厢」的说法。

normal.en: carriage of goods keeps the abstract transport sense in legal writing.
normal.cn: carriage of goods 在法律文本里保留了抽象的「货运」义。

normal.en: baby carriage is the American term for a pram.
normal.cn: baby carriage 是美式英语中的「婴儿推车」。

abstract.en: Picture four wheels, a wooden box, and two horses pulling it along a lane.
abstract.cn: 想象四个轮子、一个木箱，两匹马拉着它沿小路走。

abstract.en: Picture a train made of separate boxes linked one behind another.
abstract.cn: 想象一列火车由一节节独立盒子前后相连。

abstract.en: Picture boxes being weighed and marked before a long journey.
abstract.cn: 想象箱子在长途运输前被称重、做标记。

examples.en: The carriage moved slowly along the country road.
examples.cn: 马车沿着乡间小路慢慢走。

examples.en: We found seats in the last carriage.
examples.cn: 我们在最后一节车厢找到了座位。

examples.en: The contract covers the carriage of goods by sea.
examples.cn: 这份合同涵盖海运货物运输。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开瑞吉」——车拉着人一路往前，轮子吱吱作响。

root: 拉丁语 carrus（车）→ 晚期拉丁语 carricare（装车）→ 古法语 cariage（运送）→ 英语 carriage。

sensesIntro.en: The act of carrying becomes the vehicle that carries, on road and on rail.
sensesIntro.cn: 「运送」这个动作变成了执行运送的车辆，公路上与铁路上都是。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wheeled box being pulled along with people or goods inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个带轮盒子被人或货装满，正被拉着走。

branches.en: The road sense: a horse-drawn vehicle for passengers.
branches.cn: 公路义：由马拉的载客车辆。

branches.en: The rail sense: one passenger section of a train.
branches.cn: 铁路义：列车的一节载客车厢。

branches.en: The trade sense: the business and cost of moving goods.
branches.cn: 贸易义：运送货物的业务与费用。

branches.en: Both vehicle senses keep the same box on wheels, only the power changes.
branches.cn: 两个车辆义都是同一个带轮盒子，只是动力来源不同。

branches.en: carriage of goods survives mainly in contracts and shipping documents.
branches.cn: carriage of goods 主要保留在合同与货运单据中。

intro.en: Carriage is formed on the carrying root with the noun ending -age.
intro.cn: carriage 建立在「运送」词根上，加名词词尾 -age。

latinIntro.en: Latin carrus and carricare are the source of carriage, carry, cargo, and carrier.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carrus 与 carricare 是 carriage、carry、cargo、carrier 的共同来源。

items.meaning: a passenger vehicle or the act of transporting
items.example: The carriage stopped at the gate.

items.meaning: to take something from one place to another
a person or company that transports goods
goods carried by ship or aircraft
items.example: The cargo was checked at the port.

items.meaning: the part of a road used by vehicles
items.example: The carriageway was closed for repairs.
Carrus stands at the head of the family.
items.exampleCN: carrus 位于这个词族的最前端。

definition_zh: 吞下；忍受；燕子
definition_en: to make food or drink go down the throat, or to accept something hard
core_image: 一只燕子掠过水面，桌边的人咽下药片
scene: 他慢慢吞下那口苦药。 He slowly swallowed the bitter medicine.
sceneCN: 这里 swallow 是「吞下」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他慢慢吞下那口苦药。

derivatives.zh: 可吞服的
吞咽者

senses.title: To make something go down
senses.definition: to cause food or drink to pass down the throat
senses.definitionCN: 使食物或饮料通过喉咙
senses.example: He slowly swallowed the bitter medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 他慢慢吞下那口苦药。
senses.why: This is the basic bodily sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的身体动作义项。

senses.title: To accept something difficult
senses.definition: to accept an insult or loss without protest
senses.definitionCN: 不抗议地接受侮辱或损失
senses.example: She swallowed her anger and said nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 她忍下怒火，什么也没说。
senses.why: The throat movement becomes a metaphor for enduring.
senses.whyCN: 吞咽动作变成忍受的隐喻。

senses.title: A small bird
senses.definition: a small bird with pointed wings and a forked tail
senses.definitionCN: 一种翅尖尾叉的小鸟
senses.example: A swallow flew low over the field.
senses.exampleCN: 一只燕子低飞过田野。
senses.why: This noun is a different old word that looks the same.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是同形的另一个古老词语。

intro.en: The verb swallow is old English, while the bird name is a separate old word.
intro.cn: 动词 swallow 是古英语词，鸟名则是另一个同形的古老词。

items.en: Swelgan meant to swallow down.
items.cn: swelgan 意为吞下。

items.en: Swealwe named the bird.
items.cn: swealwe 指燕子。

items.en: Swelgan meant to swallow.
items.cn: swelgan 意为吞咽。

items.en: Swallow kept both the bird and the action.
items.cn: swallow 同时保留鸟名与动作。

items.en: Swallow also means to accept something hard.
items.cn: swallow 还表示忍受难堪之事。

note.en: Swallow is compared with look-alike words and with words for taking in.
note.cn: 把 swallow 与形近词以及表示吞入的词作比较。

not deep
to roll in mud
to swallow quickly
to eat greedily
to bear patiently

normalIntro.en: Swallow is a throat action, a way of enduring, and a bird.
normalIntro.cn: swallow 是喉咙的动作、一种忍受方式，也是一种鸟。

normal.en: He slowly swallowed the bitter medicine.
normal.cn: 他慢慢吞下那口苦药。

normal.en: She swallowed her anger and said nothing.
normal.cn: 她忍下怒火，什么也没说。

normal.en: A swallow flew low over the field.
normal.cn: 一只燕子低飞过田野。

normal.en: He swallowed hard before speaking.

normal.en: They had to swallow their pride and ask for help.
normal.cn: 他们不得不放下自尊去求助。

abstract.en: To swallow is to let something pass through without holding it.
abstract.cn: 吞咽就是让某物通过而不留住它。

abstract.en: The word makes an insult something the body must digest.
abstract.cn: 这个词把侮辱变成身体必须消化的东西。

abstract.en: A bird and an action share a shape but not a history.
abstract.cn: 一种鸟和一个动作同形，却不同源。

root: 动词来自古英语 swelgan（吞咽），名词「燕子」来自古英语 swealwe，两者同形而异源。

sensesIntro.en: Swallow means to make food go down, to bear something hard, or the bird.

definition_zh: 按字母顺序的；字母表的
definition_en: arranged according to the order of the letters of the alphabet, or relating to an alphabet
core_image: 电话簿的页面，名字从 A 一路排到 Z
scene: 前台把参会者的名牌按字母顺序摆好，方便大家快速找到自己的。 The receptionist put the name cards in alphabetical order.
sceneCN: 这里 alphabetical 是「按字母顺序的」（第 1 个义项：依照字母表先后排列）；句意是前台把名牌按字母顺序摆好。

pos.zh: 形容词：按字母顺序的；字母表的

derivatives.zh: 副词：按字母顺序地
名词：字母表，是本词的词基
动词：按字母顺序排列
形容词：字母与数字混合的

senses.title: Arranged in letter order
senses.definition: put in the sequence of the alphabet, from A towards Z
senses.definitionCN: 依照字母表从 A 到 Z 的先后排列
senses.example: The names on the register are in alphabetical order.
senses.exampleCN: 登记册上的名字按字母顺序排列。
senses.why: The suffix -ical turns alphabet into an adjective of manner, so the word says that something follows the alphabet rather than merely mentioning it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ical 把 alphabet 变成表示方式形容词，所以这个词说明某物是依照字母表排列的，而不只是提到字母表。

senses.title: Relating to an alphabet
senses.definition: connected with alphabets as writing systems, especially in contrast with picture or syllable writing
senses.definitionCN: 与作为书写系统的字母表有关，尤指区别于图画文字或音节文字
senses.example: Scholars describe the change from picture signs to alphabetical writing.
senses.exampleCN: 学者描述从图画符号到字母书写的转变。
senses.why: Because -ical also makes classifying adjectives, alphabetical can label a type of writing system, not just an order within one.
senses.whyCN: 因为 -ical 也能构成分类形容词，alphabetical 可以标示一种书写系统的类型，而不只是某系统内部的排列方式。

intro.en: Alphabetical is alphabet fitted with the Latin adjectival ending -ical.
intro.cn: alphabetical 就是 alphabet 加上拉丁形容词后缀 -ical。

items.en: The Greek name for the letter set came from alpha and beta.
items.cn: 希腊语中「整套字母」的名称来自 alpha 与 beta。

items.en: Latin kept the word as alphabetum, the base later taken into English.
items.cn: 拉丁语保留为 alphabetum，后来作为词基进入英语。

items.en: English alphabet is recorded from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语 alphabet 在十六世纪有记录。

items.en: The ending -icus formed adjectives of belonging, and English -ical continues it through French and Latin models.
items.cn: 后缀 -icus 构成表示归属的形容词，英语 -ical 经法语与拉丁语模式延续了它。

items.en: Alphabetical settled into use for lists, indexes, and dictionaries arranged by letters.
items.cn: alphabetical 在十七世纪固定用于按字母排列的清单、索引与字典。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the -ical family; the near-meaning group names other ordering principles.
note.cn: 形近组展示 -ical 词族；近义组列出其他排序原则。

normalIntro.cn: alphabet 加 -ical：表示字母顺序的形容词。

normal.en: Alphabetical order is the order you learn as a child.
normal.cn: alphabetical order 就是小时候背的那套顺序。

normal.en: The -ical ending answers the question 'in what way'.
normal.cn: -ical 结尾回答「以什么方式」。

normal.en: A dictionary is the most familiar alphabetical list.

normal.en: The adverb simply adds -ly.

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: al-pha-BET-i-cal.
normal.cn: 重音在第三个音节：al-pha-BET-i-cal。

abstract.en: Picture a phone book running from A to Z.
abstract.cn: 想象一本从 A 排到 Z 的电话簿。

abstract.en: See files lined up by their first letter.
abstract.cn: 想象文件按首字母排成一列。

abstract.en: Imagine a shelf where A comes before B.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上 A 排在 B 前面。

examples.en: Please file these reports in alphabetical order.
examples.cn: 请把这些报告按字母顺序归档。

examples.en: The glossary is alphabetical, so finding a term is quick.
examples.cn: 词汇表按字母排列，查找术语很快。

examples.en: Her surname puts her near the front of any alphabetical list.
examples.cn: 她的姓氏让她在任何字母顺序名单里都排得靠前。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective covers both the order of letters and the type of writing that uses them.

definition_zh: 奇怪地；古怪地；异常地；说来奇怪
definition_en: in a strange or unexpected way, to a surprising degree, and in the phrase oddly enough, used to introduce a fact that seems unlikely
core_image: 街角的路灯忽明忽暗，光晕一圈圈抖动着
scene: 雨夜的街角没有人，只有一盏老路灯在门边闪个不停，路人抬头看了一眼便加快脚步。 The lamp above the door behaved oddly, flickering every few seconds.
sceneCN: 这里的 oddly 是「奇怪地、古怪地」（第 1 个义项：以反常的方式）；句意为门上方那盏灯表现得很古怪，每隔几秒就闪一下。图中可辨识物件：路灯、湿地面、门边光晕。

derivatives.zh: 由古诺尔斯语 oddi（尖角、三角形）进入英语，义为「奇怪的；单数的」
由 odd 加 -ness 构成，义为「古怪；奇特」
由 odd 加 -ity 构成，义为「怪事；怪人」

senses.title: In a strange or unusual way
senses.definition: in a way that strikes other people as strange, unexpected or hard to explain
senses.definitionCN: 以让别人觉得奇怪、出乎意料或难以解释的方式
senses.example: The machine started up, then stopped oddly after a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 机器启动了，一分钟后却古怪地停了下来。
senses.why: The adjective odd first named something unmatched or off to one side, so the adverb says an action sits apart from what anyone expects.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 odd 最初指「不成对、偏在一边」的东西，因此这个副词表示某个举动与人们预想的对不上。

senses.title: To a surprising degree
senses.definition: used before an adjective to say that the quality is stronger than one would expect
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词前，表示这种性质比人们预想的更强烈
senses.example: The street was oddly quiet for a Friday night.
senses.exampleCN: 对一个星期五的夜晚来说，这条街安静得出奇。
senses.why: What is unmatched also stands out from the group, and standing out easily turns into 'more than expected', so the adverb can simply intensify.
senses.whyCN: 不成对的东西也会从群体里凸显出来，而凸显很容易转成「超出预料」，于是这个副词也能起加强作用。

senses.title: Used to introduce a surprising fact
senses.definition: used in the phrase oddly enough to bring in a fact that seems strange but is true
senses.definitionCN: 用于 oddly enough 这一说法，引出一个显得奇怪却属实的情况
senses.example: Oddly enough, nobody in the family had ever seen the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 说来奇怪，这家人竟从没有谁见过海。
senses.why: A speaker marks a fact as odd before telling it, warning listeners that the next words will not fit their expectations.
senses.whyCN: 说话的人先把这个事实标为「古怪」，再讲出来，等于提醒听的人：接下来的话不合你的预期。

intro.en: Oddly is the adverb made from odd, and odd reached English from Old Norse rather than from Latin or French; the suffix -ly simply turns the adjective into a manner word.
intro.cn: oddly 是由 odd 构成的副词，而 odd 是从古诺尔斯语而不是拉丁语或法语进入英语的；后缀 -ly 只是把形容词变成方式副词。

items.en: Oddi named a point of land, a triangle or the third, unpaired item, and the word came south with Norse settlers.
items.cn: oddi 指一块尖角地、一个三角形，或第三个落单的东西，这个词随诺尔斯移民南传。

items.en: English borrowed the form as odd and used it first for a number that cannot be paired, such as three or five.
items.cn: 英语借入该形式作 odd，最初用来指三、五这样不能两两成对的数。

items.en: Being without a partner made the word a natural label for anything left over, extra or unlike its neighbours.
items.cn: 「没有同伴」这一情况使这个词自然用来指任何剩下的、多出来的或与左邻右舍不同的东西。

items.en: From 'unlike the others' came the modern sense of strange, unusual or slightly wrong, which the nineteenth century fixed in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 由「与别的不同」生出「奇怪、反常、略有毛病」的现代义，这一用法在十九世纪的日常口语中固定下来。

items.en: Modern English uses odd for unpaired numbers, for strange things, and in informal phrases like the odd one out; oddly carries all of this into adverb form.
items.cn: 现代英语用 odd 指单数、指古怪之物，也用于 the odd one out 这类口语说法；oddly 把这些意思带进副词形式。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family that grew from odd; the near-meaning group collects other adverbs for things done or felt in an unexpected way.
note.cn: 形近组收由 odd 生长出来的词族；近义组收其他表示「以出人意料的方式」的副词。

entries.definition: Not paired with another, or strange and unexpected.
entries.definitionCN: 不成对的，或奇怪的、出人意料的。

entries.definition: A strange thing, or a person who seems unusual.
entries.definitionCN: 古怪的事物，或显得与众不同的人。

entries.definition: The quality of being strange or unlike others.
A person thought to be strange or eccentric.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为古怪、不合群的人。

entries.definition: In a way that is hard to explain or not familiar.
entries.definitionCN: 以难以解释或让人不熟悉的方式。

entries.definition: In a way that excites interest because it is unusual.
entries.definitionCN: 以因不寻常而引人好奇的方式。

entries.definition: In a way that belongs to one thing alone and is therefore odd.
entries.definitionCN: 以独特因而显得古怪的方式。

entries.definition: More than is common or expected.
entries.definitionCN: 比平常或预期更多、更强。

normalIntro.en: Oddly is odd with -ly on its back, and odd itself came in from Old Norse meaning the item left without a partner.
normalIntro.cn: oddly 是 odd 背上加了 -ly，而 odd 本身来自古诺尔斯语，指落单、没有配对的那一个。

normal.en: Oddly is simply odd plus -ly, the regular way English makes a manner adverb from an adjective.
normal.cn: oddly 就是 odd 加 -ly，是英语把形容词变成方式副词的常规做法。

normal.en: Odd first meant an unpaired number, which is why odd numbers and even numbers are still taught in pairs.
normal.cn: odd 最初指不成对的数，所以单数与偶数至今还是成对地教。

normal.en: From unpaired came the idea of unlike the rest, and from unlike the rest came the sense of strange.
normal.cn: 由「不成对」生出「与其余不同」，再由「不同」生出「奇怪」的意思。

normal.en: Oddly enough is a fixed opening: the speaker flags the surprise before delivering it.
normal.cn: oddly enough 是固定开场语：说话人先把意外标出来，再讲内容。

normal.en: Oddly quiet and oddly familiar put the adverb before an adjective to sharpen a quality, not to describe an action.
normal.cn: oddly quiet 与 oddly familiar 把副词放在形容词前，用来加强某种性质，而不是描述动作。

abstract.en: The word began with the one sock left over, which is why strangeness and loneliness sit so close in it.
abstract.cn: 这个词始于落单的那只袜子，所以「古怪」与「孤单」在它里面挨得那么近。

abstract.en: To say a thing is done oddly is to measure it against a pattern nobody wrote down.
abstract.cn: 说一件事做得古怪，就是拿它去量一个谁也没写下来的模式。

abstract.en: Oddly enough admits that the world can be true and unlikely at the same time.
abstract.cn: oddly enough 承认：世界可以同时是真的又是不大可能的。

examples.en: She smiled oddly and said nothing about the letter.
examples.cn: 她古怪地笑了笑，对那封信什么也没说。

examples.en: The room felt oddly cold in the middle of summer.
examples.cn: 盛夏里这间屋子却异常地冷。

examples.en: Oddly enough, the cheapest plan worked best.
examples.cn: 说来奇怪，最便宜的那个方案反而最管用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿得厉害」——饿得厉害了，看什么都觉得古怪；记住 oddly 是奇怪地。

root: 由 odd 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；odd 来自古诺尔斯语 oddi（尖角、三角形、落单的第三个），先指不成对的数，再指奇怪、反常。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the unpaired item standing apart from the rest; the adverb then covers odd behaviour, an odd degree of a quality, and the phrase that flags a surprise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是落单、与其余分开的那一个；副词由此覆盖古怪的举动、出奇的性质程度，以及用来标示意外的那一说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a street lamp at the corner that keeps flickering, its halo trembling.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角的路灯忽明忽暗，光晕一圈圈抖动着。

branches.en: a lamp flickering above a wet doorway
branches.cn: 湿漉漉的门上方闪个不停的灯

branches.en: a street too silent for a Friday night
branches.cn: 星期五夜里静得过分的街道

branches.en: a family that never once saw the sea
branches.cn: 一家人竟谁也没见过海

branches.en: the same sense of something not fitting the scene
branches.cn: 同一种「与场景不相称」的感觉

branches.en: an adverb placed before an adjective to sharpen it
branches.cn: 放在形容词前、用来加强它的副词

intro.en: The word is an Old Norse adjective that English adopted, then fitted with the ordinary adverb ending -ly; the rest of its family grew by adding noun suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语采用的一个古诺尔斯语形容词，再加上常规的副词后缀 -ly；词族其余成员靠加名词后缀生长。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for odd, which came into English from Old Norse and has no Latin ancestor behind it.
latinIntro.cn: odd 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，它经古诺尔斯语进入英语，背后没有拉丁语祖先。

items.meaning: a point, a triangle, an unpaired third
items.meaningCN: 尖角；三角形；落单的第三个

definition_zh: 末端的；终点的；晚期的；航站楼；终端机；终点站
definition_en: at the end of something; relating to a fatal illness; also a building or device at the end of a line
core_image: 线路尽头那扇亮灯的门
scene: 机场大厅尽头，玻璃幕墙外停着最后一班摆渡车。 Passengers waited quietly in Terminal Two.
sceneCN: 这里 terminal 是名词「航站楼」（第 4 个义项：线路或交通的终点设施）；句意：旅客在二号航站楼安静等候。

derivatives.zh: 晚期地；末端地（形容词加 -ly 构成）
终止；结束（同根动词，-ate 为动词后缀）
终点站（拉丁原词直接借入）

senses.title: At the end of something
senses.definition: placed or happening at the end of a line, journey, or structure
senses.definitionCN: 位于线、旅程或结构的末端
senses.example: The train stopped at the terminal station.
senses.exampleCN: 列车停在终点站。
senses.why: The root means boundary: whatever is terminal touches the final mark.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「界标」：凡 terminal 之物都触到了最后的界线。

senses.title: Of an illness that ends in death
senses.definition: describing an illness that cannot be cured and will cause death
senses.definitionCN: 形容无法治愈、将致死亡的疾病
senses.example: The doctor told him the illness was terminal.
senses.exampleCN: 医生告诉他病已到晚期。
senses.why: Life itself reaches its boundary; the end mark falls on the body.
senses.whyCN: 生命本身抵达界线：终点标记落在了身体上。

senses.title: A point where a line ends or meets
senses.definition: a point where wires or systems connect or end
senses.definitionCN: 线路连接或终止之点
senses.example: Check the battery terminals before starting.
senses.exampleCN: 启动前检查电池接线端。
senses.why: A boundary is also a contact point: where a line stops, another may begin.
senses.whyCN: 界线也是接触点：一条线停驻之处，另一条线可以开始。

senses.title: A building for passengers or goods at the end of a route
senses.definition: a building at an airport, port, or bus station where journeys end or start
senses.definitionCN: 机场、港口或车站里旅程开始或结束的建筑
senses.example: The airport terminal opened at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 航站楼在黎明开放。
senses.why: The endpoint of a route grows walls and roofs; the boundary becomes a place.
senses.whyCN: 路线的端点长出墙与屋顶：界线变成了场所。

senses.title: A device for entering a computer system
senses.definition: a screen and keyboard connected to a main computer or network
senses.definitionCN: 连接主机或网络的屏幕与键盘设备
senses.example: She logged in at a library terminal.
senses.exampleCN: 她在图书馆的终端机上登录。
senses.why: The device sits at the edge of the network, where the user touches the system.
senses.whyCN: 设备位于网络边缘，正是用户触碰系统之处，故称终端。

senses.title: Final and not open to change
senses.definition: final, forming the end of a series or process
senses.definitionCN: 构成系列或过程之终点的
senses.example: The court made a terminal ruling in the case.
senses.exampleCN: 法院就本案作出终局裁定。
senses.why: Once the boundary is crossed, nothing continues beyond it.
senses.whyCN: 界线一旦越过，其后便再无延续。

intro.en: Terminal comes from Latin terminalis, of a boundary, built on terminus, the boundary stone or end point.
intro.cn: terminal 源自拉丁语 terminalis「属于界标的」，词基 terminus 意为界石、端点。

items.en: Terminus was the god and the stone of boundaries in Roman fields.
items.cn: terminus 是罗马田界之神，也指界石。

items.en: Terminalis meant belonging to a boundary or end.
items.cn: terminalis 意为属于边界或端点的。

items.en: The deeper origin of terminus before Latin is uncertain; a link with words for stake or mark has been suggested.
items.cn: terminus 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定；有说法将其联系到「木桩、标记」。

items.en: English borrowed terminal in the fifteenth century for words ending a clause or a limb tip.
items.cn: 英语十五世纪借入 terminal，先指从句末词与肢体末端。

items.en: Railways gave the station sense, medicine the fatal sense, computing the device sense.
items.cn: 铁路带来终点站义，医学带来晚期义，计算带来终端机义。

note.en: Terminal is compared with its Latin family and with words of ending.
note.cn: 把 terminal 与拉丁词族及表示终结的词对比。

entries.definition: to bring to an end
the Latin word for an end point, used for final stations
the set of terms of a subject
entries.definitionCN: 术语；同一词根的另一分支

entries.definition: coming at the end
causing death
the last point of a line or process

normalIntro.en: Real links: terminus the boundary stone, the airport hall, the battery contact, and terminal illness.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：界石 terminus、机场大厅、电池接点、晚期疾病。

normal.en: Terminus was a stone at the edge of the field: terminal is anything at the edge.
normal.cn: terminus 是田边的石头：terminal 就是任何位于边缘之物。

normal.en: Terminal Two: the end of the air route has a building.
normal.cn: 二号航站楼：航线终点长出了建筑。

normal.en: Battery terminals are where the current ends and begins.
normal.cn: 电池端点是电流的终点与起点。

normal.en: A computer terminal is the edge of the network.
normal.cn: 计算机终端是网络的边缘。

normal.en: Terminal illness: the life line reaches its last mark.
normal.cn: 晚期疾病：生命之线到达最后刻度。

abstract.en: Every line owns one point where it stops pretending.
abstract.cn: 每条线都拥有一个不再假装延伸的点。

abstract.en: A boundary is a door: it can end a journey or begin one.
abstract.cn: 边界是一扇门：可以终结旅程，也可以开启旅程。

abstract.en: Endings do not always mean death; sometimes they mean arrival.
abstract.cn: 终点未必意味着死亡；有时意味着抵达。

examples.en: The ferry terminal was crowded with summer travellers.
examples.cn: 渡轮码头挤满了夏季旅客。

examples.en: New treatment gave hope even to patients with terminal illness.
examples.cn: 新疗法甚至给晚期患者带来希望。

examples.en: Loose terminals made the radio fail.
examples.cn: 接线端松动导致收音机失灵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「特米诺」——特米诺到了线路的「特末」尽头 → terminal 终点的、航站楼

root: 拉丁语 terminus「界石、端点」+ -alis → terminalis「属于边界的」→ 英语 terminal；terminate、terminus、terminology 同根。

sensesIntro.en: From boundary stone to edge marks everywhere: stations, diseases, wires, screens.
sensesIntro.cn: 从界石出发，长出各处的边缘标记：车站、疾病、电线与屏幕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone marking where the road stops.
core.cn: 核心意象：标记道路止步之处的一块石头。

branches.en: Routes end in buildings that hold the boundary.
branches.cn: 路线终结于承载边界的建筑。

branches.en: The body reaches its own boundary stone.
branches.cn: 身体抵达自己的界石。

branches.en: Where a line ends, contact begins.
branches.cn: 线止之处，接触开始。

branches.en: The user sits at the network's edge.
branches.cn: 用户坐在网络边缘。

branches.en: A ruling that closes the file for good.
branches.cn: 一笔永久归档的终局裁定。

intro.en: Terminal heads the terminus family of boundary words.
intro.cn: terminal 是 terminus「边界」词族之首。

latinIntro.en: Latin terminus, boundary stone, gave terminalis and the whole family of end words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 terminus「界石」生出 terminalis 与整个「终点」词族。

definition_zh: 熟人；了解；相识
definition_en: a person you know slightly, or knowledge of a subject
core_image: 街角遇见一张熟悉的脸，彼此点头，却叫不出全名
scene: 在车站，我碰见了一位多年不见的熟人。 I met an old acquaintance at the station.
sceneCN: 这里的 acquaintance 是「熟人」（第 1 个义项：认识但不深交的人）；句意是我在车站遇到一位旧识。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「使熟悉」
由动词加过去分词词尾构成，义为「熟悉的」
由名词加抽象名词后缀构成，义为「相识关系」

senses.title: A person known slightly
senses.definition: someone you have met and recognize but do not know well
senses.definitionCN: 见过面、认得出来、但并不熟悉的人
senses.example: She is an acquaintance from my old office.
senses.exampleCN: 她是我以前办公室的一位熟人。
senses.why: The noun ending names a person rather than the act, so acquaintance becomes the face you know by name but not by heart.
senses.whyCN: 名词词尾把它指成一个人，而不是动作，于是 acquaintance 成了那个你知道名字、却不深知的人。

senses.title: Knowledge of a subject
senses.definition: a working knowledge of a field or a body of facts
senses.definitionCN: 对某个领域或一批事实的实用了解
senses.example: His acquaintance with old maps helped the search.
senses.exampleCN: 他对古地图的了解帮上了搜寻的忙。
senses.why: Knowing a person and knowing a subject are the same Latin root, so the noun also means a first-hand familiarity with facts.
senses.whyCN: 认识人与认识学问共用同一个拉丁词根，所以这个名词也指对事实的第一手熟悉。

senses.title: The relationship of knowing
senses.definition: the state of having met and being known to one another
senses.definitionCN: 彼此见过面、互相知道对方的这种关系
senses.example: Their acquaintance began at a summer school.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的相识始于一次暑期学校。
senses.why: Between the person and the knowledge lies the relation itself, and English lets the same noun name that thin thread.
senses.whyCN: 在人与其所知之间还横着关系本身，英语就让同一个名词也指这根细细的线。

intro.en: The noun is the French form of a Latin knowing verb, with a noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个名词是拉丁语「知道」动词的法语形式，再加名词词尾。

items.en: cognoscere meant to get to know.
items.cn: cognoscere 意为逐渐认识。

items.en: acointier meant to make someone known to another.
items.cn: acointier 意为使某人被另一人认识。

items.en: the noun acointance named the state of knowing someone.
items.cn: 名词 acointance 指认识某人的状态。

items.en: acquaintance entered English for both the person and the relation.
items.cn: acquaintance 在十四世纪进入英语，兼指那个人与那种关系。

items.en: the countable sense, a person, is now the most common.
items.cn: 如今最常用的是可数义，也就是「一个熟人」。

note.en: The first group is the acquaint family; the second is other words for people one knows.
note.cn: 第一组是 acquaint 词族；第二组是别的表示认识之人的词。

entries.definition: to make familiar
having knowledge of
a slight relationship
the act of familiarizing
a person one works or deals with
a person one can reach
knowledge of something
a person who works with you

normalIntro.en: The word is the noun twin of acquaint, built on the Latin root for knowing.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 acquaint 的名词孪生兄弟，建在拉丁语「知道」词根上。

normal.en: acquaint is to make known, acquaintance is the one who is known.
normal.cn: acquaint 是使知道，acquaintance 是被认识的那个人。

normal.en: make the acquaintance of is the formal way to say meet.
normal.cn: make the acquaintance of 是「结识」的正式说法。

normal.en: a casual acquaintance is someone you greet but do not confide in.
normal.cn: casual acquaintance 是点头打招呼、却不会交心的人。

normal.en: acquaintance with facts is the uncountable, abstract use.
normal.cn: acquaintance with facts 是不可数的抽象用法。

normal.en: the plural acquaintances simply lists several such people.
normal.cn: 复数 acquaintances 只是列出好几个这样的人。

abstract.en: See a familiar face across the platform and a quick wave.
abstract.cn: 想象站台对面一张熟悉的脸，和你飞快地挥一下手。

abstract.en: Picture a name tag you can read but a story you cannot tell.
abstract.cn: 想象胸牌上的名字你看得清，他的故事你却讲不出。

abstract.en: Think of a thin thread linking two people who never quite became friends.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细线连着两个人，他们始终没真正成为朋友。

examples.en: He is an acquaintance rather than a close friend.
examples.cn: 他是熟人，而不是密友。

examples.en: Her acquaintance with Chinese poetry surprised the class.
examples.cn: 她对中国古诗的了解让全班吃惊。

examples.en: They struck up an acquaintance during the long delay.
examples.cn: 在漫长的延误中，他们结识了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿昆腾斯」——阿昆在站台遇见熟人，热络地腾出一个座位。

root: 古法语 acointance，源自 acointier（使认识），再上溯拉丁语 cognoscere（知道）；本义是「相识的状态」，后指认识而不深交的人。

sensesIntro.en: One noun names the person, the knowledge and the thin relation between them.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个名词，分别指那个人、那份了解，以及两者之间那根细线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a known face with an unknown story.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张认得的脸，一段不知道的故事。

branches.en: the person you greet but do not confide in
branches.cn: 会打招呼却不会交心的人

branches.en: a working knowledge of maps or poetry
branches.cn: 对地图或古诗的实用了解

branches.en: the relation that starts at a summer school
branches.cn: 始于暑期学校的那种关系

branches.en: a person and the tie that holds him
branches.cn: 一个人以及牵着他的那根线

branches.en: knowing a subject and knowing a face
branches.cn: 懂一门学问与认得一张脸

intro.en: The French verb stem plus a noun ending gives the person and the state.
intro.cn: 法语动词词干加名词词尾，给出人与状态两种意思。

latinIntro.en: The knowing root cognoscere also yields recognize and cognition.
latinIntro.cn: 「知道」词根 cognoscere 也产生 recognize 与 cognition。

definition_zh: 矿石；矿料
definition_en: rock or earth that contains enough metal or valuable mineral to be worth mining and processing
core_image: 矿车从黑洞里推出来，车斗里的石头带着细小的金属光泽
scene: 山脚的旧矿口塌了半边，地面散着带锈色的碎石，工人蹲下去敲了敲。 A truck hauled the ore down the valley road.
sceneCN: 这里是「矿石」（第 1 个义项：天然产出、含金属的岩石）；句意为卡车把矿石沿山谷公路运下去。图中可辨识物件：矿口、锈色碎石、矿车。

derivatives.zh: 由 ore 与 body 复合而成，义为「矿体」
由 ore 与 bearing 复合而成，义为「含矿的」
由 ore 与 forming 复合而成，义为「成矿的」

senses.title: Rock that contains metal
senses.definition: rock or earth from which a metal or other valuable mineral can be extracted at a profit
senses.definitionCN: 能从中经济地提炼金属或其他有用矿物的岩石、土石
senses.example: The mine produces copper ore of unusually high grade.
senses.exampleCN: 这座矿出产品位异常高的铜矿石。
senses.why: The Old English word named metal still lying unworked in the ground, so ore begins as the metal-bearing material before any fire touches it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语里这个词指仍躺在地里、未经加工的金属，所以 ore 的起点是尚未经过炉火的含金属物料。

senses.title: The mined material sent for smelting
senses.definition: the material as dug out and prepared for transport or smelting, rather than the deposit left in the ground
senses.definitionCN: 已经被采出、准备运输或冶炼的物料，而不是仍留在地下的矿藏
senses.example: Conveyors carried the ore from the shaft to the washing plant.
senses.exampleCN: 传送带把矿料从井口送到洗选厂。
senses.why: Once the rock leaves the shaft it is no longer part of the deposit but a load to be handled, and English keeps the same word for what trucks and ships carry.
senses.whyCN: 岩石一旦离开井口，就不再是矿藏的一部分，而成了要搬运的货物；英语对卡车和船装的这批东西仍用同一个词。

intro.en: Ore is a native Germanic word for metal still in the ground; its earliest forms are reconstructed and some details remain uncertain.
intro.cn: ore 是英语本土的日耳曼词，指仍在地里的金属；它最早的形态是重构出来的，部分细节仍有争议。

items.en: The reconstructed root *uz- is generally linked to the idea of out or up, which fits metal coming out of the earth; the exact development is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *uz- 与「向外、向上」的意思相关，正合金属从地里出来的画面；具体演变仍有争议。

items.en: Old English ora named ore or unworked metal, and it is the earliest recorded form of the word in English.
items.cn: 古英语 ora 指矿石或未经加工的金属，是这个词在英语中最早见于记录的形态。

items.en: Middle English ore settled into the modern spelling and the meaning of metal-bearing rock.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ore 固定为今天的拼写，含义是「含金属的岩石」。

items.en: As mining and smelting grew, the word was fixed in compounds such as iron ore and copper ore and in the trade of ore dressing.
items.cn: 随着采矿与冶炼发展，这个词固定在 iron ore、copper ore 等复合词里，也进入选矿这一行当的说法。

items.en: Modern English uses ore mainly for the raw feed of a smelter, and geologists add compounds such as orebody and ore grade.
items.cn: 现代英语的 ore 主要指送进冶炼厂的原料，地质学者又添出 orebody、ore grade 这类说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that sound or look close to ore and marks their different origins; the near-meaning group collects mining and mineral words.
note.cn: 形近组收发音或拼写接近 ore 的词，并注明它们来源不同；近义组收采矿与矿物方面的词。

entries.definition: A pole with a blade, used to row a boat.
entries.definitionCN: 带桨叶、用来划船的桨；与 ore 只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A conjunction used to link alternatives.
entries.definitionCN: 连接两个选项的连词；与 ore 只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A continuous mass of ore within the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 地下连续成块的矿体，由 ore 与 body 复合而成。

entries.definition: A natural solid substance such as quartz or iron pyrites.
entries.definitionCN: 石英、黄铁矿之类的天然固体物质；矿物。

entries.definition: A layer of material that has built up in the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 在地下积成的一层物料；矿床、沉积层。

entries.definition: A hard shiny material such as iron or copper.
entries.definitionCN: 铁、铜之类坚硬有光泽的物质；金属。

normalIntro.en: Ore is a single Germanic root with no Latin twin, so the mnemonics stay with the picture of metal-bearing rock coming out of the ground.
normalIntro.cn: ore 是一个没有拉丁孪生词的日耳曼词根，所以联想始终围绕「含金属的岩石从地里出来」的画面。

normal.en: Ore is a Germanic word, not a Latin one, and its oldest recorded form is Old English ora.
normal.cn: ore 是日耳曼词而不是拉丁词，它最早的记录形态是古英语 ora。

normal.en: The reconstructed root behind it points to something coming out of the earth, which is what ore is.
normal.cn: 它背后的重构词根指向「从地里出来的东西」，而矿石正是这样。

normal.en: Iron ore and copper ore fix the word to particular metals in everyday use.
normal.cn: iron ore 与 copper ore 把这个词和具体金属固定在一起。

normal.en: An orebody is ore plus body: a body of ore inside the rock.
normal.cn: orebody 是 ore 加 body：岩石里面的一团矿体。

normal.en: Ore grade measures how much metal a load of ore carries, a phrase straight from mining.
normal.cn: ore grade 衡量一批矿石含多少金属，是直接从矿业里来的说法。

abstract.en: A cart of broken rock rolling out of darkness with a faint shine on its face.
abstract.cn: 一车碎矿石从暗处滚出来，表面带着一点微光。

abstract.en: What makes rock worth carrying is not its weight but the metal hidden inside it.
abstract.cn: 让岩石值得搬运的不是它的重量，而是藏在里面的金属。

abstract.en: Everything solid we build with was once part of a hole in a hillside.
abstract.cn: 我们用来建造的一切坚硬东西，都曾是山坡上一个洞里的东西。

examples.cn: 卡车把矿石沿山谷公路运下去。

definition_zh: 海的；海洋的；海生的；航海的；（名词）海军陆战队员
definition_en: relating to the sea, living in the sea, or connected with shipping and naval forces; as a noun, a soldier trained to serve at sea and on coasts
core_image: 退潮后的礁池里，海藻贴着石面，小蟹在浅水里横着走
scene: 退潮后的礁石间满是海藻和小蟹，是一处微缩的海洋群落。 Between the rocks at low tide lived seaweed and crabs, a marine community in miniature.
sceneCN: 这里 marine 指「海洋的、海生的」（第 2 个义项：生活在海中的生物群落）；句意：退潮后的礁石间住着海藻与小蟹，是一个微缩的海洋群落。图中可辨识物件：礁池、贴石的海藻、小蟹、退潮留下的水线；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Of the sea as an environment
senses.titleCN: 海洋环境的、与海有关的
senses.definition: relating to the sea as a physical environment, including its water, floor and shores
senses.definitionCN: 与作为物理环境的海洋有关，包括海水、海底与海岸
senses.example: The marine environment absorbs a large share of human carbon emissions.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋环境吸收了人类碳排放的很大一部分。
senses.why: Latin mare means sea, so the adjective marks the sea as a setting for any process, not only for living things.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 mare 意为「海」，因此这个形容词标记海洋作为任何过程的场景，而不只用于生物。

senses.title: Living in the sea
senses.definition: describing plants and animals that live in salt water, especially in open sea habitats
senses.definitionCN: 描述生活在咸水中、尤指开阔海域生境的动植物
senses.example: Between the rocks at low tide lived seaweed and crabs, a marine community in miniature.
senses.exampleCN: 退潮后的礁石间住着海藻与小蟹，是一个微缩的海洋群落。
senses.why: the adjective attaches to the organism by its medium, and marine contrasts with freshwater and terrestrial.
senses.whyCN: 形容词按介质附着于生物，marine 与 freshwater、terrestrial 形成对照。

senses.title: Connected with shipping and seafaring
senses.definition: relating to ships, navigation and commerce by sea
senses.definitionCN: 与船舶、航行和海上贸易有关
senses.example: Marine insurance covers cargo lost overboard in heavy weather.
senses.exampleCN: 海运保险承保恶劣天气中落水的货物。
senses.why: sea transport is the oldest commercial use of the sea, so marine became the standard adjective in shipping and insurance law.
senses.whyCN: 海上运输是海洋最古老的商业用途，因此 marine 成为航运与保险法中的标准形容词。

senses.title: Naval and marine forces
senses.definition: relating to naval forces, especially soldiers trained to fight at sea or on coasts
senses.definitionCN: 与海军力量有关，尤指受训在海上或海岸作战的士兵
senses.example: Marine units were the first to reach the flooded port.
senses.exampleCN: 海军陆战队是最先抵达被淹港口的部队。
senses.why: the noun marine 'soldier serving at sea' arose because such troops belong to the sea service, so the adjective and the soldier share one form.
senses.whyCN: 名词 marine「在海上服役的士兵」之所以出现，是因为这类部队属于海上军种，因此形容词与士兵同名。

senses.title: Of the sea floor and its deposits
senses.definition: describing sediments, rocks and layers formed on or under the sea floor
senses.definitionCN: 描述在海底或海底之下形成的沉积物、岩石与层理
senses.example: Marine sediments record thousands of years of climate change.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋沉积物记录了几千年的气候变化。
senses.why: geology needed a term for deposits laid down by water, and marine specifies salt-water basins rather than lakes.
senses.whyCN: 地质学需要指「由水沉积」的术语，marine 则进一步限定为咸水盆地而非湖泊。

senses.title: Moderate climate influenced by the sea
senses.titleCN: 受海洋调节的（海洋性气候）
senses.definition: describing a climate with small temperature swings because the sea moderates the air above it
senses.definitionCN: 描述因海洋调节其上方空气而温差较小的气候
senses.example: The island's marine climate keeps winters mild and summers cool.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的海洋性气候使冬天温和、夏天凉爽。
senses.why: climatology applies the sea adjective to places whose weather is dominated by nearby water, in contrast with continental climates.
senses.whyCN: 气候学把「海」的形容词用于受近海支配的天气，与大陆性气候相对。

senses.title: Of marine science as a discipline
senses.definition: used for the scientific study of the sea, as in marine biology, marine chemistry and marine geology
senses.definitionCN: 用于海洋科学研究，如海洋生物学、海洋化学与海洋地质学
senses.example: The station runs a marine science programme for local schools.
senses.exampleCN: 该站为本地学校开设海洋科学课程。
senses.why: each sea-related discipline prefixed its name with marine, making the adjective a stable label for a whole field.
senses.whyCN: 各门与海有关的学科都在名称前加 marine，使该形容词成为整个领域的稳定标签。

senses.title: A soldier of the marine corps
senses.definition: a member of a military force trained for operations at sea, on coasts and in amphibious landings
senses.definitionCN: 受训执行海上、海岸与两栖登陆作战任务的军人
senses.example: Two marines guarded the gangway while the cargo was checked.
senses.exampleCN: 货物检查时，两名陆战队员守着舷梯。
senses.why: the noun is a shortened form of marine soldier, and it survives as the everyday name of the corps in several navies.
senses.whyCN: 该名词是 marine soldier 的缩略，至今仍是若干海军中这支兵种的日常称呼。

intro.en: Marine comes from Latin marinus 'of the sea', from mare 'sea'. English borrowed it through Old French in the fifteenth century, and the soldier sense followed in the seventeenth.
intro.cn: marine 来自拉丁 marinus「海的」，源于 mare「海」。英语经古法语在 15 世纪借入，士兵义在 17 世纪随后出现。

items.en: Mare was the ordinary Latin word for sea. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and the Indo-European form sometimes cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: mare 是拉丁语中表示「海」的常用词。其更深来源不确定，有时为其引用的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: Marinus 'of the sea' was formed from mare, and it described sea creatures, sea water and sea-going matters.
items.cn: marinus「海的」由 mare 构成，用于描述海洋生物、海水与航海事务。

items.en: Old French marin brought the adjective into English around 1400, first in natural history and then in shipping.
items.cn: 古法语 marin 在 15 世纪初把该形容词带入英语，最初见于博物学，随后进入航运。

items.en: In the seventeenth century marine was used as a noun for soldiers raised to serve aboard ships, the origin of the modern marine corps.
items.cn: 17 世纪，marine 用作名词，指招募到舰上服役的士兵，这是现代海军陆战队的源头。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century oceanography prefixed its subfields with marine, fixing the adjective in names such as marine biology and marine geology.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪的海洋学给各分支冠以 marine，使该形容词固定出现在 marine biology、marine geology 等名称中。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin history of mare is unsettled, and the earliest English citation is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：mare 在拉丁语之前的历史无定论，英语最早书证的年代也只能大致确定。

note.en: Group one distinguishes marine from same-root words for sailors, harbours and sea law, and from a look-alike with a different root; group two contrasts it with other sea-related adjectives.
note.cn: 第一组把 marine 与同根却指水手、码头、海事法的词区分开，并辨明一个词根不同的形近词；第二组对照其它与海有关的形容词。

entries.definition: A sailor; it comes from Latin marinarius through French, so it shares mare but names a person, not a habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 水手；经法语来自拉丁 marinarius，与 mare 同源，但指人而非生境。

entries.definition: A basin for pleasure boats; the -a ending makes it a place, while marine is the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 供游艇停泊的小港；-a 词尾使它指场所，而 marine 是形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to the sea in law, trade and defence; from Latin maritimus, it is the formal legal cousin of marine.
entries.definitionCN: 在法律、贸易与防务上与海有关的；来自拉丁 maritimus，是 marine 的正式法律近亲。

entries.definition: Relating to marriage; it comes from Latin maritus 'husband', not mare 'sea', so the resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 与婚姻有关的；来自拉丁 maritus「丈夫」而非 mare「海」，因此形近只是巧合。

entries.definition: Relating to the open ocean, especially far from coasts; marine is broader and includes shelves and shores.
entries.definitionCN: 与开阔大洋有关，尤指远离海岸；marine 范围更广，包含陆架与海岸。

entries.definition: Relating to a navy and its ships; marine covers civil and biological senses as well.
entries.definitionCN: 与海军及其舰船有关的；marine 还覆盖民用与生物义。

entries.definition: Relating to sailors, ships and navigation; it stresses seamanship rather than the sea itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与水手、船舶和航行有关的；它强调航海术而非海洋本身。

entries.definition: Describing salty water or organisms in it; it names the chemical condition that marine assumes.
entries.definitionCN: 描述咸水或其中的生物；它点明 marine 所预设的化学条件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real mare root, real derivatives and real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 mare 词根、真实派生词与真实搭配。

normal.en: Mare is Latin for sea, and it survives in marine, mariner, marina and maritime.
normal.cn: mare 是拉丁语的「海」，仍见于 marine、mariner、marina、maritime。

normal.en: Marine life, marine ecosystem and marine biology are the standard biology collocations.
normal.cn: marine life、marine ecosystem、marine biology 是生物学的标准搭配。

normal.en: Marine insurance and marine law keep the shipping sense alive in legal English.
normal.cn: marine insurance 与 marine law 让航运义在法律英语中延续。

normal.en: The proper noun Marine Corps explains why a soldier is simply 'a marine'.
normal.cn: 专名 Marine Corps 解释了为什么士兵直接被称为 a marine。

normal.en: Marine climate is the climatology partner of continental climate.
normal.cn: marine climate 是大陆性气候在气候学中的配对词。

abstract.en: Picture a tide pool that holds an entire ocean's logic in a bowl of water.
abstract.cn: 想象一个潮池，用一盆水装下整片大洋的逻辑。

abstract.en: Picture a cargo crate whose insurance policy never leaves the shore.
abstract.cn: 想象一只货箱，它的保单从未离开海岸。

abstract.en: Picture a soldier trained on a beach, halfway between land and sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一名在海滩受训的士兵，站在陆地与海洋之间。

examples.en: Marine plastic debris accumulates in mid-ocean gyres.
examples.cn: 海洋塑料垃圾在洋流环流中积聚。

examples.en: The marine climate keeps the island green through winter.
examples.cn: 海洋性气候让这座岛整个冬天保持绿色。

examples.en: Marines secured the dock before the aid ships arrived.
examples.cn: 海军陆战队员在救援船到达前控制了码头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mare（海）+ ine」——mare 是海，marine 就是「海的、海里的」；大写 Marine 又一跃成了陆战队员

root: 拉丁 marinus「海的」= mare「海」+ -inus（形容词后缀）；mare 的更深来源不确定。英语 marine；同族有 mariner、maritime、marina。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one body of salt water: the sea as environment, the life in it, shipping, naval troops, sea-floor deposits, sea-moderated climate, marine science, and finally the soldier whose name is the noun form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一片咸水辐射开来：作为环境的海洋、其中的生命、海运、海军部队、海底沉积、受海调节的气候、海洋科学，最后是以名词形式出现的陆战队员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the salt sea as a place, a medium and a service.
core.cn: 核心意象：咸海既是场所，也是介质，也是服役对象。

branches.en: SEA AS HABITAT: the adjective marks both the setting and the organisms in it.
branches.cn: 海作为生境：形容词既标场景，也标其中的生物。

branches.en: SEA AS ROUTE: shipping and insurance turn the sea into infrastructure.
branches.cn: 海作为航线：航运与保险把海变成基础设施。

branches.en: SEA AS SERVICE: naval troops and the marine corps make the adjective a rank and a noun.
branches.cn: 海作为军务：海军部队与陆战队使形容词兼作军种名与名词。

branches.en: SEA AS OBJECT OF STUDY: sediments and marine science name what is examined.
branches.cn: 海作为研究对象：沉积物与海洋科学指出被考察之物。

branches.en: SEA AS CLIMATE FORCE: nearby water moderates the air above it.
branches.cn: 海作为气候力量：近旁的水调节其上方的空气。

intro.en: Marine is built on the Latin noun mare 'sea' plus -inus; the same root yields mariner, marina, maritime and the submarine, while sub- and mariculture extend it in modern technical words.
intro.cn: marine 由拉丁名词 mare「海」加 -inus 构成；同一词根衍生 mariner、marina、maritime 与 submarine，而 sub- 与 mariculture 在现代技术词中加以扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin mare 'sea', marinus 'of the sea' and maritimus 'of the coast' are the core ancestors of the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mare「海」、marinus「海的」与 maritimus「海岸的」是这一英语词族的核心祖形。

items.example: Mare is the base of the whole English sea family.
items.exampleCN: mare 是整个英语「海」词族的基础。

items.example: Marinus means belonging to the sea.
Marine algae anchor the coastal food web.
items.exampleCN: 海洋藻类支撑着海岸食物网。

items.example: The mariner read the sky before setting out.
The marina sheltered twenty small boats.
items.exampleCN: 游艇码头停泊着二十条小船。

items.meaning: relating to the sea in law and trade
items.example: Maritime law governs the salvage claim.
items.exampleCN: 海事法管辖这项打捞请求。

items.meaning: a vessel that travels under the sea
items.example: The submarine surfaced beyond the reef.
items.exampleCN: 潜艇在礁石外浮出水面。

items.example: Mariculture rafts cover the sheltered bay.
items.exampleCN: 海水养殖筏铺满受庇护的海湾。

items.example: She studied marine biology at the coastal station.
items.exampleCN: 她在海岸观测站学习海洋生物学。

definition_zh: 神话；神话故事；神话体系；广为相信的谬见；虚构的人或事；编造的托词
definition_en: a traditional story about gods or origins, or a widely believed but false idea
core_image: 夜里的火堆旁，老人用手比划着天与地如何分开，听的人明知不是真的却仍点头
scene: 火堆旁，老人把陶罐放在膝上，向围坐的孩子讲起天和地最初如何分开。 An old storyteller recounts the myth of how sky and earth were separated.
sceneCN: 这里 myth 指「关于神或世界起源的传统故事」（第 1 个义项：世代相传的神话叙事）；句意为一位老讲述者讲述天与地如何分开的神话。可辨识物件：火堆、陶罐、围坐的孩子、夜色；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 神话；神话故事；神话体系；谬见；虚构的人或事

derivatives.zh: 基础词 myth + -ic（形容词后缀）→ 由「神话故事」偏移为「具有神话气质的、传奇般的」
基础词 myth + -ical（形容词后缀）→ 偏移为「只存在于神话中、虚构的」
基础词 myth + 希腊 -logia（「讲述、研究」）→ 由「一则故事」偏移为「神话的整体汇集与研究」
mythology + -ist（人名词后缀）→ 偏移为「研究神话的学者」
mythology + -ize（动词后缀）→ 由「神话」偏移为「把某人某事讲成神话」
mythologize + -ation（动作名词后缀）→ 偏移为「被讲成神话的过程」
myth + maker（英语复合，表制造者）→ 偏移为「编造神话或制造流行谬见的人」

senses.title: A traditional tale of gods
senses.titleCN: 关于神与起源的传统故事
senses.definition: a traditional story, usually concerning gods or the origin of the world, passed on by a community
senses.definitionCN: 通常在讲神或世界起源、由群体世代相传的传统故事
senses.example: The myth tells how the first fire was carried down from the mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 这则神话讲的是最初的火如何从山上被带下来。
senses.why: the Greek noun meant a thing spoken aloud, so a myth is first of all a story that a community keeps telling.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊名词原指被大声讲出来的东西，所以神话首先是一个群体不断讲述的故事。

senses.title: A body of myths
senses.definition: the whole collection of such stories belonging to one culture or subject
senses.definitionCN: 属于某一文化或主题的这类故事的整体汇集
senses.example: The myth of the region is preserved mainly in oral chant.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的神话主要靠口头吟唱保存。
senses.why: the singular noun can stand for a whole tradition, the way a library name stands for all its books.
senses.whyCN: 单数名词可以代表整个传统，就像一座图书馆的名字代表它的全部藏书。

senses.title: A widely believed falsehood
senses.definition: an idea that many people accept as true although it has been shown to be false
senses.definitionCN: 许多人信以为真、但已被证明为假的说法
senses.example: It is a myth that we use only a tenth of the brain.
senses.exampleCN: 「人只用了大脑的十分之一」是一种谬见。
senses.why: a story that everyone repeats can harden into something people treat as fact, and English extended the same noun to that kind of false belief.
senses.whyCN: 一个被所有人反复讲述的故事会硬化成人们当作事实的东西，英语便把同一个名词扩展到这类错误信念上。

senses.title: A fabricated person or thing
senses.definition: a person or thing that exists only in imagination or in a story
senses.definitionCN: 只存在于想象或故事中的人或物
senses.example: The feared pirate turned out to be a myth invented by the port's guides.
senses.exampleCN: 那个令人惧怕的海盗后来证明是港口导游编出来的虚构人物。
senses.why: a figure that exists only because it is talked about is the same product as a story, with a face attached.
senses.whyCN: 一个只因为被谈论才存在的人物，与一个故事是同一种产物，只是给它安上了一张脸。

senses.title: A made-up excuse
senses.definition: an invented account offered to explain or excuse something
senses.definitionCN: 为解释或开脱某事而编出来的说法
senses.example: His story about a delayed train was pure myth.
senses.exampleCN: 他那套火车误点的说法纯属编造。
senses.why: an excuse is a short story offered in place of the facts, so the same noun serves when the telling is deliberate.
senses.whyCN: 托词是一则用来代替事实的短故事，因此当讲述是故意为之，同一个名词就派上了用场。

senses.title: A category of narrative
senses.titleCN: 神话作为叙事类型（学术用语）
senses.definition: the class of narrative that scholars set apart from legend, folktale and history
senses.definitionCN: 学者用来与传说、民间故事和历史相区分的那类叙事
senses.example: In this discipline, myth is defined by its concern with origins, not by its being false.
senses.exampleCN: 在这门学科里，神话是由它关注起源来定义的，而不是由它虚假来定义的。
senses.why: scholars needed a neutral label for the genre, so the noun was kept but stripped of the everyday judgement that a myth is simply untrue.
senses.whyCN: 学者需要给这一文类一个中性的标签，于是保留了这个名词，却去掉了日常语言里「神话就是假的」那层判断。

senses.title: A legendary figure
senses.titleCN: 传奇式人物，被神化的偶像
senses.definition: a person who has been talked about so much that the telling has replaced the person
senses.definitionCN: 被谈论得太多、以致讲述取代了本人的人物
senses.example: By the end of his career the boxer had become a myth in his own city.
senses.exampleCN: 到职业生涯末期，这位拳手在自己城市里已经成了一个传奇。
senses.why: when the telling grows larger than the person, the story takes over the identity, and the noun names the figure that remains.
senses.whyCN: 当讲述大过本人，故事便接管了这个身份，名词所指的就是剩下的那个形象。

senses.title: A story a society tells itself
senses.definition: a shared narrative that a society uses to explain or justify its own arrangements
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会用来解释或为自己制度辩护的共同叙事
senses.example: The frontier myth still shapes how the country explains its history.
senses.exampleCN: 边疆神话至今仍在塑造这个国家解释自身历史的方式。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the story element but shifts the function: the tale now explains the tellers to themselves.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了故事成分，却换了功能：故事现在用来向讲述者自己解释他们自身。

intro.en: Myth comes from Greek mythos 'word, speech, story', borrowed into Late Latin and then into modern languages; English took it through French in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: myth 来自希腊 mythos「言语、讲述、故事」，先借入晚期拉丁，再进入近代诸语言；英语经法语在十九世纪引入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mythos covered 'word, speech, thing said, tale'. It could mean a public pronouncement as much as a narrative, so speech and story were one idea.
items.cn: mythos 涵盖「言语、讲述、所说之事、故事」，既可指公开宣告，也可指叙事，说话与故事在当时是一个概念。

items.en: Philosophers set mythos against logos, the reasoned account, and from that contrast mythos acquired the overtone of an unproved story.
items.cn: 哲学家把 mythos 与 logos（理性论证）对立起来，自此 mythos 带上「未经证明的故事」这一色彩。

items.en: Late Latin took mythos as a learned borrowing; it was not an inherited Latin noun and had no Latin relatives of its own.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁把 mythos 作为学术借词吸收；它不是拉丁语固有名词，也没有自身的拉丁同族词。

items.en: French mythe carried the learned word into modern use, and English myth followed in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 mythe 把这个学术词带入近代用法，英语的 myth 随后在十九世纪出现。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the noun widened from sacred tales to any widely repeated falsehood, a sense now commoner than the original one.
items.cn: 在十九与二十世纪，这个名词从神圣故事扩展到任何被广泛重复的错误说法，这一义项如今比原义更常用。

items.en: Source uncertain: the origin of mythos before Greek is not established, and no Indo-European source has been demonstrated; any older form proposed for it is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 来源不确定：mythos 在希腊语之前的来源未得到证明，也没有任何印欧语来源被证实；凡为它提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates myth from the story genres it is confused with; group two holds the everyday words for untrue or unproved accounts.
note.cn: 第一组把 myth 与常被混淆的故事文类分开；第二组是表示「不实、未经证明」的日常词。

entries.definition: A story about a human hero, often attached to a real place or person; myth deals with gods and origins, legend keeps a historical foothold.
entries.definitionCN: 关于人类英雄的故事，常附着于真实地点或人物；神话处理神与起源，传说则保留历史落脚点。

entries.definition: A story told among ordinary people, often for entertainment or moral instruction; it lacks the sacred and explanatory role of myth.
entries.definitionCN: 在普通民众间讲述的故事，多用于娱乐或教化；它没有神话那种神圣与解释的作用。

entries.definition: A short invented story, often with animals, that points to a moral; it is openly fictional and didactic.
entries.definitionCN: 常以动物为主角的短小虚构故事，指向一条道理；它公开承认虚构并带训诫性。

entries.definition: A collection of myths or the study of them; myth is one story, mythology is the set or the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 神话的汇集或对神话的研究；myth 是一则故事，mythology 是整套或这门学科。

entries.definition: The Greek word itself, used in English for the underlying pattern of a myth or for a group's shared story-world.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊原词本身，在英语中用来指一则神话的底层模式，或一个群体共享的故事世界。

entries.definition: A mistaken understanding held by many people; it names the error plainly, without the story image that myth carries.
entries.definitionCN: 许多人持有的错误理解；它直白地指错误，不含 myth 所带的故事意象。

entries.definition: A statement that is not true, whether or not anyone believes it; myth adds wide acceptance.
entries.definitionCN: 不真实的陈述，无论是否有人相信；myth 则多了「被广泛接受」这一层。

entries.definition: Something invented on purpose to deceive; it implies intent, while a myth's false sense often implies only repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 为欺骗而故意编造的东西；它含故意，而 myth 的谬见义常只含反复流传。

entries.definition: The state of holding something as true; a myth may become a belief, but belief itself says nothing about stories.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事当作真的状态；神话可以变成信念，但 belief 本身与故事无关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek elements, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek mythos 'a thing said': a myth is literally something a community keeps saying aloud.
normal.cn: 希腊 mythos「被说出的东西」：神话字面上就是一个群体不断大声讲的东西。

normal.en: The family runs myth, mythic, mythical, mythology, mythologist, mythologize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 myth、mythic、mythical、mythology、mythologist、mythologize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark both senses: ancient myth, Greek myth, and the myth of progress.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出两层意思：古老神话、希腊神话，以及关于进步的虚妄信念。

normal.en: Greek kept mythos and logos as a pair: story against reasoned account.
normal.cn: 希腊语把 mythos 与 logos 当作一对：故事对理性论证。

normal.en: The academic use says myth concerns origins, so a myth can be true to its tellers and still be a myth.
normal.cn: 学术用法说神话关注起源，因此一则神话对讲述者可以为真，却仍然是神话。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence that gets heavier each time it is repeated, until it can no longer be lifted.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话每被重复一次就重一点，最后重得抬不起来。

abstract.en: Picture a portrait repainted by every visitor until the original face is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅肖像被每位来客添改，最后原来的脸已经不见了。

abstract.en: Picture a map drawn from memory and then used as if it were the ground itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一张凭记忆画的地图，后来被当成地面本身来使用。

examples.en: The myth explains why the river turns salt where it meets the sea.
examples.cn: 这则神话解释了那条河为什么在人海处变咸。

examples.en: It is a myth that older workers cannot learn new software.
examples.cn: 「年长的员工学不会新软件」是一种谬见。

examples.en: The film turns a minor local trader into a myth of resistance.
examples.cn: 这部影片把一个微不足道的本地商人塑造成了抵抗的传奇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「myth（音近『秘思』）」——被反复讲述、越传越神秘的那套说法 → 神话；也指广为相信的谬见

root: 希腊 mythos「言语、讲述、故事」，先作学术借词进入晚期拉丁，再经法语进入英语；mythos 更早来源不确定，无已证实的印欧语来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: something gets told and retold, and the retelling first makes a sacred story, then a whole story-world, then a false belief, an invented person, an excuse, a genre label, a legendary figure, and finally a society's account of itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：某件事被讲了又讲，这反复讲述先造出神圣故事，再造出整套故事世界，随后造出谬见、虚构人物、托词、文类标签、传奇人物，最后造出一个社会对自身的解释。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tale retold around a fire until the retelling stands where the fact used to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：火堆旁被一遍遍重讲的故事，讲到后来，重讲本身站在了事实原来的位置上。

branches.en: THE TALE AND THE SET: one story first, then the whole body of stories a culture keeps.
branches.cn: 故事与整套：先是一则故事，再是一个文化保存的整批故事。

branches.en: REPETITION WITHOUT PROOF: an often-repeated tale turns into a false belief, and an invented account becomes an excuse.
branches.cn: 无凭据的重复：被反复讲述的故事变成错误信念，编出来的说法变成托词。

branches.en: PERSONS MADE OF TALK: a thing or a person can be wholly produced by the telling.
branches.cn: 由讲述造出的人与物：一件东西或一个人可以完全由讲述生产出来。

branches.en: A NEUTRAL GENRE LABEL: scholars keep the noun but drop the judgement that a myth must be false.
branches.cn: 中性的文类标签：学者保留这个名词，却去掉「神话必然虚假」这一判断。

branches.en: THE STORY A SOCIETY TELLS ITSELF: the tale now explains the tellers to themselves.
branches.cn: 社会讲给自己的故事：故事此时用来向讲述者解释他们自身。

intro.en: Myth is a bare Greek noun in English, but it builds a large family through suffixes that name studies, qualities, persons and processes.
intro.cn: myth 在英语里是一个光裸的希腊名词，但它通过指学科、性质、人物与过程的后缀建起一个很大的词族。

latinIntro.en: No Latin family stands behind myth. Latin took mythos only as a Greek loanword, so there is no inherited Latin cognate to list.
latinIntro.cn: myth 背后没有拉丁词族。拉丁语只把 mythos 当作希腊借词吸收，因此没有可列的拉丁固有同族词。

items.example: The myth survived in three versions.
items.exampleCN: 这则神话以三个版本留存下来。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into a quality word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成性质词。

items.example: The longer suffix sounds more formal.
items.exampleCN: 较长的后缀听起来更正式。

items.example: The striker became a mythic name.
items.exampleCN: 这位前锋成了神话般的名字。

items.example: A mythical harbour appears on the old chart.
items.exampleCN: 旧海图上出现一个神话中的港口。

items.meaning: the set of myths or their study
items.meaningCN: 神话的整体或对神话的研究
items.example: She teaches the mythology of northern Europe.

items.exampleCN: 这位神话学者编目了各种异文。
回忆录作者会把自己的青年时代写成神话。

items.example: The mythologization of the founder began at his funeral.
items.exampleCN: 对创始人的神话化从他的葬礼就开始了。

items.meaning: one who invents myths or false beliefs
items.exampleCN: 每个时代都有自己的神话制造者。

definition_zh: 水龙头；旋塞；出水口
definition_en: a device that controls the flow of water from a pipe, its valve, or the spout where the water comes out
core_image: 厨房水槽上方的金属龙头，一滴水正挂在出水口，久久没有落下
scene: 他拧开水龙头，接了一杯凉水。 She turned the faucet and filled a glass with cold water.
sceneCN: 这里 faucet 是「水龙头」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她拧开水龙头，接了一杯凉水。

derivatives.zh: 水龙头（英式）
龙头；塞子

senses.title: A water tap
senses.definition: a device that lets water out of a pipe when opened
senses.definitionCN: 打开后能让水从管道流出的装置
senses.example: The kitchen faucet is dripping again.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房的水龙头又滴水了。
senses.why: This is the common American sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是该词在美式英语中最常见的含义。

senses.title: A valve controlling flow
senses.definition: the valve inside such a device that opens or closes the flow
senses.definitionCN: 装置内部控制水流开闭的阀门
senses.example: Turn the faucet clockwise to shut off the water.
senses.exampleCN: 顺时针转动旋塞就能关掉水。
senses.why: The visible handle works a valve, and the word names both.
senses.whyCN: 可见的把手操控阀门，而该词同时指称两者。

senses.title: The water outlet
senses.definition: the spout or outlet where water leaves the pipe
senses.definitionCN: 水离开管道的喷嘴或出口
senses.example: She held the cup under the faucet.
senses.exampleCN: 她把杯子放在出水口下方。
senses.why: The part people see and use most is the spout itself.
senses.whyCN: 人们最常看到和使用的部分就是出水口。

intro.en: Faucet comes from Old French fausset, a bung or stopper, probably linked to faux, false.
intro.cn: faucet 源自表示塞子的古法语 fausset，可能和 faux（虚假的）有关。

items.en: Falsus meant false or deceptive.
items.cn: falsus 意为虚假的、骗人的。

items.en: Fausset named a bung used to stop a cask.
items.cn: fausset 指用来塞住木桶的塞子。

items.en: The word crossed into English use for a pipe stopper.
items.cn: 该词传入英语，指管道塞子。

items.en: Faucet named a tap or spout for liquid.
items.cn: faucet 指放出液体的龙头或喷嘴。

items.en: American English made faucet the everyday word for a tap.
items.cn: 美式英语中 faucet 成为水龙头的日常说法。

note.en: Faucet is compared with similar-looking words and with words for taps and valves.
note.cn: 把 faucet 与形近词以及表示龙头、阀门的词作比较。

entries.definition: one side or aspect of something
the passage at the back of the mouth
relating to the throat
a device for controlling water, used in British English
a small tap or stopper for a barrel
a part that controls the flow of liquid or gas

normalIntro.en: Faucet is the American word for a tap and the valve behind it.
normalIntro.cn: faucet 是美式英语中的水龙头，也指其内部阀门。

normal.en: British speakers usually say tap instead of faucet.
normal.cn: 英国人通常说 tap，而不是 faucet。

normal.en: A dripping faucet wastes water.
normal.cn: 滴水的龙头会浪费水。

normal.en: Faucet and facet differ by one letter.
normal.cn: faucet 和 facet 只差一个字母。

normal.en: Turn the faucet off after washing your hands.
normal.cn: 洗完手后要关掉水龙头。

normal.en: The hot faucet carries water from the heater.
normal.cn: 热水龙头输送来自热水器的水。

abstract.en: A stopper became a spout as plumbing changed.
abstract.cn: 随着管道技术进步，塞子变成了出水口。

abstract.en: One fixture holds a handle, a valve, and an outlet.
abstract.cn: 一件龙头装置同时包含把手、阀门与出水口。

abstract.en: American and British words can split one simple object.
abstract.cn: 美式与英式说法会把同一个简单物件分成两个词。

examples.en: The faucet in the bathroom leaks.
examples.cn: 浴室的水龙头漏水。

examples.en: Please turn off the faucet after use.
examples.cn: 用完后请关掉水龙头。

examples.en: A plumber replaced the old faucet.
examples.cn: 水管工换掉了旧龙头。

dict_mnemonic.text: faucet 经古法语 fausset（塞子）进入英语，最初指管道的塞子，后来专指控制水流的水龙头。

root: 源自拉丁语 falsus（虚假的）经古法语 fausset（塞子），核心义「控制管道水流的装置」。

sensesIntro.en: Faucet means a water tap, the valve that controls it, or the spout where water comes out.
sensesIntro.cn: faucet 意为水龙头、控制水流的阀门，或出水的喷嘴。

core.en: A household device that starts and stops the flow of water.
core.cn: 控制水流开启与关闭的家用装置。

branches.en: The whole fixture people turn on and off.
branches.cn: 人们开关的整套龙头装置。

branches.en: The inner valve that controls the flow.
branches.cn: 内部控制水流的阀门。

branches.en: The spout where the water leaves.
branches.cn: 水流出的喷嘴。

branches.en: The fixture and its outlet are seen as one object.
branches.cn: 装置与出水口被视为同一个物件。

branches.en: Turning the fixture means working the valve inside.
branches.cn: 转动龙头就是操作内部的阀门。

intro.en: Faucet has few derived forms, so related plumbing words fill out the family.
intro.cn: faucet 的派生形式很少，因此用相关管道词汇补足词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin falsus and Old French fausset stand behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 falsus 与古法语 fausset 是该词的历史来源。

items.example: The faucet is beside the sink.
The hotel replaced all the faucets.
items.exampleCN: 酒店更换了所有水龙头。

items.meaning: the British word for a faucet
items.example: Turn the tap to the left.
The old taps were made of brass.
He opened the spigot on the barrel.
items.exampleCN: 他打开了木桶上的龙头。

items.example: The pipes end in brass spigots.
items.exampleCN: 管道末端装着黄铜龙头。

items.example: The valve must be closed first.

items.exampleCN: 水管工检查了两个阀门。

definition_zh: 柔韧的；灵活的；可变通的
definition_en: able to bend easily without breaking, or able to change to suit new conditions
core_image: 一根软管绕过桌角，弯了却不断
scene: 这根软管很柔韧，可以绕过拐角。 The hose is flexible enough to bend around the corner.
sceneCN: 这里 flexible 是「柔韧的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这根软管很柔韧，可以绕过拐角。

derivatives.zh: 灵活性；柔韧性
灵活地
僵硬的

senses.title: Bends easily
senses.definition: able to bend without breaking
senses.definitionCN: 能够弯曲而不断裂的
senses.example: The hose is flexible enough to bend around the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 这根软管很柔韧，可以绕过拐角。
senses.why: This is the physical sense of bending.
senses.whyCN: 这是弯曲的物理义项。

senses.title: Open to change
senses.definition: able to change plans when needed
senses.definitionCN: 需要时能够改变计划的
senses.example: My schedule is flexible this week.
senses.exampleCN: 我这周的日程很灵活。
senses.why: A schedule that can bend is called flexible.
senses.whyCN: 能弯曲的日程被称为灵活。

senses.title: Adaptable
senses.definition: able to be used in different ways
senses.definitionCN: 能以不同方式使用的
senses.example: The room has a flexible layout.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间的布局很灵活。
senses.why: Tools that adjust to many uses are flexible.
senses.whyCN: 能适应多种用途的工具是灵活的。

senses.title: Willing to compromise
senses.definition: willing to change a position in discussion
senses.definitionCN: 在讨论中愿意改变立场的
senses.example: We need a flexible negotiator.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要一位能变通的谈判者。
senses.why: A rigid view cannot bend toward agreement.
senses.whyCN: 僵硬的立场无法向共识弯曲。

intro.en: Flexible comes from Latin flexibilis, able to be bent, from flectere, to bend.
intro.cn: flexible 源自拉丁语 flexibilis（可弯曲的），来自 flectere（弯曲）。

items.en: Flectere meant to bend or turn.
items.cn: flectere 意为弯曲或转向。

items.en: Flexibilis meant able to be bent.
items.cn: flexibilis 意为可被弯曲的。

items.en: Flexibilitas named the quality of bending.
items.cn: flexibilitas 指可弯曲的性质。

items.en: Flexible described bendable materials.
items.cn: flexible 描述可弯曲的材料。

items.en: The word extended to plans and people.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到计划与人。

note.en: Flexible is compared with similar-looking words and with words for bending and adapting.
note.cn: 把 flexible 与形近词以及表示弯曲和适应的词作比较。

entries.definition: an automatic body response
constant change
a muscle that bends a joint
able to stretch and return
easy to bend
able to adjust

normalIntro.en: Flexible is the quality of a thing or a mind that can bend and still come back.
normalIntro.cn: flexible 是物体或头脑能弯曲又能恢复的性质。

normal.en: Rubber is flexible.
normal.cn: 橡胶有柔韧性。

normal.en: We keep a flexible schedule.
normal.cn: 我们保持灵活的日程。

normal.en: The furniture has a flexible design.
normal.cn: 这件家具有灵活的设计。

normal.en: A flexible teacher adapts to the class.
normal.cn: 灵活的老师会适应班级情况。

normal.en: Inflexible rules cause delay.
normal.cn: 僵硬的规则造成延误。

abstract.en: What can bend survives what breaks the rigid.
abstract.cn: 能弯曲的东西能挺过让僵硬者折断的事。

abstract.en: Flexibility is a form of strength.
abstract.cn: 灵活是一种力量。

abstract.en: A tree that bends keeps its roots.
abstract.cn: 会弯的树保住了根。

examples.en: The hose is flexible enough to bend around the corner.
examples.cn: 这根软管很柔韧，可以绕过拐角。

examples.en: My schedule is flexible this week.
examples.cn: 我这周的日程很灵活。

examples.en: The room has a flexible layout.
examples.cn: 这个房间的布局很灵活。

dict_mnemonic.text: flexible 源自拉丁语 flectere（弯曲）加 -ibilis（可……的），字面即「可弯曲的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 flectere（弯曲），核心义「能被弯曲而不折断」。

sensesIntro.en: Flexible means able to bend, to change plans, to serve many uses, or to compromise.
sensesIntro.cn: flexible 意为柔韧的、灵活改变计划的、多用途的或愿变通的。

core.en: Able to bend and still hold.
core.cn: 能弯曲而仍保持完好。

branches.en: Material that bends without cracking.
branches.cn: 弯曲而不裂的材料。

branches.en: A schedule that can shift.
branches.cn: 可以调整的日程。

branches.en: A design used in many ways.
branches.cn: 可多种方式使用的设计。

branches.en: A person who can move toward agreement.
branches.cn: 能向共识靠拢的人。

branches.en: Materials and plans bend alike.
branches.cn: 材料与计划以同样方式弯曲。

intro.en: Flexible belongs to the Latin flect- family of bending words.
intro.cn: flexible 属于拉丁语 flect- 这一表示弯曲的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin flectere and flexibilis supply the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 flectere 与 flexibilis 提供整个词族。

items.exampleCN: 柔韧性在年老时很有用。

items.example: Flexion of the knee is painful.

definition_zh: 不利的；有害的；反对的；相反的
definition_en: unfavorable to success or well-being, or opposed and contrary to something
core_image: 帆船正顺风前行，一股逆向的侧风突然把船身推离航线
scene: 登山队刚出发不久，山脊上就压来一片铅灰色的云。 The climb was called off because of adverse weather.
sceneCN: 这里的 adverse 是「不利的」（第 1 个义项：对顺利与安全有害的）；句意为由于天气恶劣，攀登被取消。

pos.zh: 形容词：不利的；有害的；反对的；相反的

derivatives.zh: 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「不利地；有害地」
由同一词根构成，义为「逆境；不幸」
由拉丁语 adversarius 而来，义为「对手；敌手」
加形容词后缀 -ial 构成，义为「对抗性的」

senses.title: Against one's interests
senses.definition: harmful to success, health, or well-being, or making a good result less likely
senses.definitionCN: 对成功、健康或福祉有害的，或使好结果更难出现的
senses.example: Heavy rain had an adverse effect on the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨对收成产生了不利影响。
senses.why: ad- means towards and vertere means to turn, so adversus is 'turned towards' in a hostile way: an adverse force has turned round to face you.
senses.whyCN: ad- 表示朝向，vertere 表示转，adversus 是「转过来对着」，即掉头冲着你来的力量，所以 adverse 指不利。

senses.title: Opposed in opinion
senses.definition: not in favour of a plan, proposal, or position, and acting or speaking against it
senses.definitionCN: 不赞成某项计划、提议或立场的，并加以反对的
senses.example: The board remained adverse to any rise in membership fees.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会仍然反对提高任何会员费。
senses.why: The same turning image moves from events to the will: when someone is adverse to a proposal, their attitude has swung round to face it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「转身」的意象从事件转到意志上：说一个人 adverse to 某提议，就是他的态度已转过来对着它。

intro.en: One Latin verb of turning grows into a word for whatever turns against us.
intro.cn: 一个表示「转」的拉丁动词，长成了指称「掉头与我们作对之物」的词。

items.en: vertere meant to turn, and it underlies a large family: versus, reverse, convert and vertigo all turn in some way.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，它支撑起一大族词：versus、reverse、convert 与 vertigo 都带「转」的意思。

items.en: ad 'towards' plus versum 'turned' gave adversum, a phrase meaning 'towards, facing', which could turn hostile.
items.cn: ad（向）加 versum（转过的）构成 adversum，本指「朝向、面对」，也可以带出敌对的意味。

items.en: As an adjective adversus meant 'opposite, contrary, hostile'; as a noun, an adversary was the person facing you.
items.cn: 作形容词时 adversus 意为「对面的、相反的、敌对的」；作名词时指「面对着你的人」，即敌手。

items.en: Old French passed the adjective into English in the sense of contrary fortune or opposing circumstance.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词传入英语，当时多指「相反遭际」或「对立情形」。

items.en: English records adverse from the fourteenth century; the modern phrase adverse effect dates from later technical writing.
items.cn: 英语自十四世纪起记录 adverse；现代常用的 adverse effect 则来自较晚的专业文献。

items.en: Today the word is most at home before nouns such as effect, weather and reaction, marking whatever works against a good outcome.
items.cn: 今天它最常放在 effect、weather、reaction 这类名词前，标记一切与好结果作对的因素。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root of turning; the second collects common words for what works against us.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「转」的拉丁词根；第二组收几个表示「与人作对」的常用词。

entries.definition: a difficult or unlucky situation; misfortune
an opponent in an argument, contest, or conflict
in a way that harms or works against something
to turn away or prevent something bad; same turning root, other prefix
entries.definitionCN: 避免；转移；同词根但前缀不同

entries.definition: not likely to produce a good result; the plain opposite of favourable
entries.definitionCN: 不利的；不妙的；favourable 的反义词

entries.definition: causing damage, especially to health; more physical than adverse
entries.definitionCN: 有害的；尤指对健康造成损害，比 adverse 更具体

entries.definition: openly unfriendly or opposed; stronger in feeling than adverse
entries.definitionCN: 敌对的；敌意的；情绪比 adverse 更强烈

entries.definition: causing harm or damage; a formal synonym common in reports
entries.definitionCN: 有害的；造成损害的；报告体常用

normalIntro.en: Three real pieces carry the word: ad-, vertere and the adjective ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由三个真实部件构成：ad-、vertere 与形容词词尾。

normal.en: ad- is towards and vertere is to turn, so adverse is turned against you.
normal.cn: ad- 是「朝向」，vertere 是「转」，adverse 就是转过来对着你。

normal.en: The same root gives versus, reverse and convert, all words of turning.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 versus、reverse、convert，都是「转」的词。

normal.en: adverse effect is the commonest pairing in medical and business writing.
normal.cn: adverse effect 是医学与商业文本里最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Do not confuse adverse with averse; averse describes a person's dislike.
normal.cn: 别把 adverse 与 averse 混用，averse 说的是人「不喜欢」。

normal.en: Spell it with -verse, the same ending as reverse.
normal.cn: 拼写是 -verse，和 reverse 的结尾一样。

abstract.en: Picture a sail turning flat against the wind, and the boat losing speed.
abstract.cn: 想象帆面转过来迎着风，船立刻慢下来。

abstract.en: See a row of arrows all pointing at one small figure on a map.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上一排箭头全部指向一个很小的人影。

abstract.en: Imagine a door that keeps swinging shut in your face, however often you open it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，你每推开一次，它都朝你脸上关回来。

examples.en: The drug may cause adverse effects in older patients.
examples.cn: 这种药可能在老年患者身上引起不良反应。

examples.en: Farmers struggled through a season of adverse conditions.
examples.cn: 农民在整整一季的不利条件中艰难支撑。

examples.en: She remained adverse to the idea of moving abroad.
examples.cn: 她仍然反对搬到国外去的想法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱德沃斯」——爱德沃斯一遇逆风就掉头，处处跟他作对。

root: 拉丁语 adversus 由 ad-「朝向」与 vertere「转」构成，本义是「转过来对着、敌对的」，经古法语进入英语后专指「不利的、相反的」。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses share one image of turning: circumstances turn against you, or a person's will turns against a proposal.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项共用一个「转身」的意象：要么环境掉头与你作对，要么人的意志掉头反对某项提议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sail swings round and faces the wind, and the boat loses way.
core.cn: 核心意象：帆面转过来迎风，船随即失去速度。

branches.en: weather that pushes a climb off its route
branches.cn: 把登山计划推离路线的天气

branches.en: a vote that swings against a proposal
branches.cn: 转而反对提案的表决

branches.en: a drug acting against the body it should help
branches.cn: 与身体作对的药物

branches.en: a fixed hostile stance in a debate
branches.cn: 辩论中固定的敌对立场

branches.en: one turning root, used for events and for attitudes
branches.cn: 同一个「转」的词根，既用于事件也用于态度

intro.en: A prefix of direction, a Latin verb of turning, and ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: 一个方向前缀、一个表示「转」的拉丁动词，加上普通的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: vertere and adversus are recorded Latin; only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: vertere 与 adversus 都是有文献记录的拉丁词，只有更早的印欧词根属重构。

definition_zh: 双胞胎之一；成对的；使成对
definition_en: one of two children born at the same time, or either of a matching pair
core_image: 两张一模一样的脸并排睡着，呼吸几乎同步
scene: 婴儿床里并排放着两个小篮子，两顶同样的小帽子挨在一起。 Her twin brother lives in the next street.
sceneCN: 这里 twin 是「双胞胎之一」（第 1 个义项：同时出生的两个孩子中的一个）；句意为她的双胞胎哥哥住在隔壁那条街。两张一模一样的脸，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 twin 加 -ing 构成，义为「结为姊妹城市；成对」
由 twin 加 -ed 构成，义为「结成姊妹的；成对的」
由 twin 加指小词尾构成，义为「双生的小东西」

senses.title: The matching child
senses.definition: one of two children born to the same mother at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 同一位母亲在同一次生产中产下的两个孩子之一
senses.example: Her twin brother lives in the next street.
senses.exampleCN: 她的双胞胎哥哥住在隔壁那条街。
senses.why: The word names one half of a pair that nature made at the same moment.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名一对同时被自然造出的孩子中的一半。

senses.title: The matching pair
senses.definition: used before a noun for one of two things that are alike or joined
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，指两件相似或相连的事物之一
senses.example: The twin towers stood at the harbour mouth.
senses.exampleCN: 双塔立于港口入口。
senses.why: Anything that comes in a matching pair can carry the word as a label.
senses.whyCN: 凡成双成对的东西都能用这个词作标签。

senses.title: The linking act
senses.definition: to join two things closely, as towns or schools are paired
senses.definitionCN: 把两者紧密联结，如城市或学校结为姊妹单位
senses.example: The town is twinned with a village in Italy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇与意大利的一个村庄结为姊妹城镇。
senses.why: If nature can produce a pair, people can also decide to make one, so the verb means to pair.
senses.whyCN: 自然能生出成对之物，人也能决定造出一对，于是动词表「配成对」。

intro.en: Twin is a Germanic word meaning two together, closely related to the words for two and twilight.
intro.cn: twin 是日耳曼语中「两个一起」的词，与 two、twilight 关系密切。

items.en: The root meant a pair or a double thing born together.
items.cn: 这个词根意为成对或同时出生的两件物。

items.en: Twinn meant double, and getwinn meant a pair of twins.
items.cn: twinn 意为双的，getwinn 意为双生的一对。

items.en: Twin came to name one child of such a pair.
items.cn: twin 转而指这样一对中的一个孩子。

items.en: Shapes, rooms and towers borrowed the word for anything matching.
items.cn: 形状、房间、高塔都借这个词表示成对。

items.en: The verb appeared with town twinning after the war.
items.cn: 战后同城结对使人看到它的动词用法。

note.en: The first group shares the two-ness of the stem, the second names pairs and doubles.
note.cn: 第一组共享词干里的「二」，第二组是成双、成对的词。

entries.definition: Cord of twisted threads.
The pair together.
To wind or turn something.
Two of the same kind.
Two things that go together.
An exact copy.

normalIntro.en: Twin has two in it, both in sound and in sense.
normalIntro.cn: twin 的声音和意思里都装着「二」。
