definition_zh: 偏见；成见；使有偏见；损害
definition_en: a preconceived opinion formed without adequate grounds, or to bias someone or to harm a right or interest
core_image: 一叠贴好标签的档案袋，还没打开就已经判定了内容
scene: 招聘会上，一名主管看到简历上的外地学校名称，就把材料放到一边。 The trainer calls that reflex prejudice rather than a hiring rule.
sceneCN: 这里 prejudice 指「未经充分了解就形成的成见」（第 1 个义项：预先形成、缺乏依据的看法）；句意为培训师把那种反射式的反应称为偏见，而非招聘规则。场景要素：简历堆、标签、被推到一边的文件夹；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 使有偏见；损害（权利、机会）

collocations.zh: 不影响法律权利地；不损及权益

derivatives.zh: 由 prejudice 加过去分词词尾构成，指自己抱有偏见的
由 prejudice 加形容词后缀构成，指会造成损害的
由否定前缀加 prejudiced 构成，指不带偏见的
由表「在前」的前缀加 judge 构成，指事先就作出判断

senses.title: An opinion formed without adequate grounds
senses.definition: a judgment about someone or something made before the facts are known
senses.definitionCN: 在了解事实之前就对某人某物作出的判断
senses.example: Her prejudice about the neighbourhood faded after a single afternoon there.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那个街区的成见，在待了一个下午之后就淡了。
senses.why: The Latin noun means a judgment made beforehand, so the word records not hatred but the timing of the judgment.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁名词意为「事先作出的判断」，因此这个词记录的不是仇恨，而是判断的时点。

senses.title: Hostility toward a group
senses.definition: a hostile or unfair orientation toward people because of the group they belong to
senses.definitionCN: 因某人所属的群体而对其持有的敌意或不公取向
senses.example: The report documented prejudice against migrant workers in hiring.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了招聘中对外来务工人员的偏见。
senses.why: A pre-judgment aimed at a whole category turns into hostility, and this is the sense most people mean today.
senses.whyCN: 针对整个类别的预先判断会变成敌意，这也是今天多数人所指的义项。

senses.title: A favourable pre-judgment
senses.definition: a pre-judgment that can lean in someone's favour as well as against them
senses.definitionCN: 一种可能有利于某人、也可能不利于某人的预先判断
senses.example: His prejudice in favour of old buildings made him miss the mould in the basement.
senses.exampleCN: 他对老房子的偏爱让他忽略了地下室的霉斑。
senses.why: English keeps the neutral frame, so the word can describe a favourable lean, which is why 'prejudice in favour of' still occurs.
senses.whyCN: 英语保留了中性框架，因此这个词可以形容有利的倾斜，「偏爱」的说法至今仍在用。

senses.title: To bias someone's mind
senses.titleCN: 使某人的判断带上偏向
senses.definition: to cause someone to form an opinion in advance of the evidence
senses.definitionCN: 使某人在证据出现之前就形成看法
senses.example: The leaked summary prejudiced the panel before it heard a witness.
senses.exampleCN: 提前流出的摘要让评审团在听证之前就有了倾向。
senses.why: The verb turns the state into an act: someone or something does the pre-judging to another mind.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个状态变成动作：某人或某物把预先判断做进了另一个头脑。

senses.title: To harm a right or interest
senses.definition: to damage or impair a legal right, a claim or a chance
senses.definitionCN: 损害或削弱某项法律权利、主张或机会
senses.example: The delay prejudiced the tenant's claim to compensation.
senses.exampleCN: 这拖延损害了租客获得补偿的主张。
senses.why: Law generalised the word from a wrong opinion to any action that puts a right at a disadvantage.
senses.whyCN: 法律把这个词从「错误的看法」推广到任何使权利处于不利地位的行为。

senses.title: A dismissal that bars refiling
senses.definition: in procedure, a final dismissal of a claim that prevents it being brought again
senses.definitionCN: 程序上对某项主张的终局驳回，使其不得再次提出
senses.example: The case was dismissed with prejudice after the plaintiff failed to appear.
senses.exampleCN: 原告未出庭后，案件以终局方式驳回。
senses.why: A final ruling 'prejudges' the matter for good, which is why the old word survives in this narrow procedural formula.
senses.whyCN: 终局裁决等于把这件事实地预先判定了，因此这个古老的词在这条狭窄的程序套语里留存。

senses.title: A social attitude distinct from behaviour
senses.titleCN: 与社会行为相区别的态度
senses.definition: in social psychology, an attitude toward a group, studied separately from discriminatory acts
senses.definitionCN: 社会心理学中，对某群体的态度，与歧视行为分开研究
senses.example: Prejudice and discrimination are measured as attitude and action, not as one thing.
senses.exampleCN: 偏见与歧视被分别测作态度与行为，而不是同一件事。
senses.why: The discipline needed to split the inner leaning from the outward act, so the word was fixed to the inner side.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科需要把内心的倾斜与外显的行为分开，于是把这个词固定在内心一侧。

senses.title: To the detriment of someone
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase, to the disadvantage or injury of a person or interest
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法中，指使某人或某种利益处于不利或受损
senses.example: The new route was chosen to the prejudice of the fishing village.
senses.exampleCN: 新路线被选中，代价是渔村受损。
senses.why: The prepositional phrase keeps the harm sense alive outside courtrooms, where it means damage in plain speech.
senses.whyCN: 这个介词短语把损害义留在法庭之外，日常言谈中它就指造成的损失。

intro.en: Prejudice comes through Old French from Latin praejudicium 'a judgment beforehand', built from a prefix meaning 'before' and the noun for judgment. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: prejudice 经古法语来自拉丁语 praejudicium「事先的判断」，由表「在前」的前缀与表「判断」的名词构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: The prefix meant 'before, in front', and it fixes the timing of the judgment in the word itself.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为「在前、在之前」，它把判断的时点固定在词里。

items.en: Judicium meant a declaring or a ruling, built on judex 'judge', itself from law plus the verb for declaring.
items.cn: judicium 意为宣告或裁断，建立在 judex「法官」之上，而后者又由「法律」与表「宣告」的动词构成。

items.en: The compound named a preliminary ruling and, in ordinary use, an opinion formed before the case was heard.
items.cn: 这个复合名词指初步裁决，在日常用法中也指在听取案件之前就形成的看法。

items.en: Old French prejudice carried both the legal and the mental senses into English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把这个词的法律义与心智义一并带入英语。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word narrowed toward hostility between groups, and psychology later separated it from discrimination.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词向群体间的敌意收窄，心理学后来把它与歧视区分开。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): the earliest English use is recorded only approximately, and the pre-Latin origin of the word for law is unsettled, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：最早的英语用例只有约略记载；那个表「法律」的词在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words and adjectives that are routinely mixed up with the noun; group two holds near neighbours for a group-directed attitude.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词，以及常与本名词弄混的形容词；第二组是表示针对群体的态度的近义词。

entries.definition: Describes a person who holds a prejudice; the noun names the prejudice itself, and the two are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容人抱有偏见；名词指偏见本身，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: Means likely to cause damage to a right or a case; it does not mean full of prejudice.
entries.definitionCN: 意为很可能损害某项权利或案件，并不表示「充满偏见」。

entries.definition: A ruling or a formed opinion without the prefix, so it says nothing about whether the opinion came too early.
entries.definitionCN: 不带该前缀的裁决或看法，因此并不表明这个看法是否来得太早。

entries.tag: the verb built with the same prefi
entries.definition: To judge before hearing the evidence; it is the act that produces a prejudice.
entries.definitionCN: 指在听取证据之前就判断，正是产生偏见的行为。

entries.definition: Any leaning, often unconscious and sometimes harmless; prejudice implies an unfair or unfounded leaning.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何偏向，往往无意识且有时无害；prejudice 暗示不公或缺乏依据。

entries.definition: Treating people differently in practice; psychology keeps it separate from the inner attitude that prejudice names.
entries.definitionCN: 指实际行为上的区别对待；心理学把它与 prejudice 所指的内心的态度分开。

entries.definition: A simplified image of a group; a stereotype can supply the content of a prejudice but is not itself hostility.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某群体的简化形象；它可为偏见提供内容，但本身不是敌意。

entries.definition: Stubborn intolerance of another group, stronger and more openly hostile than prejudice.
entries.definitionCN: 指对另一群体的顽固不容忍，比 prejudice 更强、更公开敌意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the real judging root, the real family and the real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、表「判断」的词根、真实的词族与真实的法律说法。

normal.en: The prefix means before and the base means judgment, so prejudice is a judgment that arrives before the facts.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「在前」，基底意为「判断」，因此偏见就是赶在事实之前到达的判断。

normal.en: The family runs judge, judgment, judicial, prejudice, prejudiced, prejudicial, prejudge.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 judge、judgment、judicial、prejudice、prejudiced、prejudicial、prejudge。

normal.en: Legal phrases preserve the harm sense: without prejudice, dismissed with prejudice, to the prejudice of.
normal.cn: 法律说法保存了损害义：不损及权益、以终局方式驳回、损害……的利益。

normal.en: The adjective prejudiced describes a person, while prejudicial describes something harmful.
normal.cn: 形容词 prejudiced 形容人，而 prejudicial 形容有害之物。

normal.en: Social psychology separates the attitude from the act, calling them prejudice and discrimination.
normal.cn: 社会心理学把态度与行为分开，分别称为偏见与歧视。

abstract.en: Picture a folder labelled before it has been opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一个还没打开就已经贴好标签的文件夹。

abstract.en: Picture a lens ground before the optician has measured the eye.
abstract.cn: 想象磨好的镜片，而验光师还没量过眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a gavel that falls before the witness is sworn.
abstract.cn: 想象法槌在证人宣誓之前就落下了。

examples.en: The campaign measured prejudice through questions about hiring and housing.
examples.cn: 这场运动通过招聘与住房方面的问题来测量偏见。

examples.en: Reading one bad review prejudiced him against the whole school of thought.
examples.cn: 读了一篇差评，就让他对整个学派有了成见。

examples.en: The ruling was issued without prejudice to either party's further claims.
examples.cn: 该裁定不损及双方后续的主张。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pre 在前 + judge 判断」——还没看清就先判了，就是偏见

root: 拉丁 praejudicium「事先的判断」由意为「在前」的前缀加 judicium（裁断，出自 judex「法官」= jus「法律」+ dicere「宣告」）；jus 更深来源不确定。英语 prejudice。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one early judgment: a verdict is reached before the evidence arrives. It is read as an unfounded opinion, as hostility toward a group, as a favourable lean, as the act of biasing a mind, as harm to a right, as a final dismissal, as an attitude studied apart from behaviour, and as a plain phrase for damage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「提前的判断」展开：证据未到，裁决先落。它依次被读作缺乏依据的看法、对群体的敌意、有利的倾斜、使他人带上偏向的行为、对权利的损害、终局驳回、与行为分开研究的态度，以及日常说法中的损失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of folders already labelled before any is opened.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠档案袋还没打开，标签就已经贴好。

branches.en: THE PRE-JUDGMENT: an unfounded opinion and a favourable one share the same timing, which is the real subject of the word.
branches.cn: 预先的判断：缺乏依据的看法与有利的看法共享同一个时点，时点才是这个词真正的主题。

branches.en: FROM OPINION TO ENMITY: when the early judgment is aimed at a whole group, it hardens into hostility.
branches.cn: 从看法到敌意：当提前的判断对准整个群体，它就硬化为敌意。

branches.en: DOING IT TO A MIND: the verb marks the moment one person's lean is planted in another.
branches.cn: 做进别人脑中：动词标出某人的倾斜被栽进另一个人头脑的那一刻。

branches.en: HARM: legal impairment and the everyday phrase for damage both turn a wrong opinion into a lost right.
branches.cn: 损害：法律上的削弱与日常说到损失的说法，都把错误的看法变成失去的权利。

branches.en: FIXED IN PLACE: a dismissal that bars refiling and an attitude studied apart from action both keep the first judgment from moving.
branches.cn: 固定原位：不得再诉的驳回与与行为分开研究的态度，都让最初的判断无法移动。

intro.en: Prejudice is a Latin prefix plus the same judging noun that builds judge and judgment, so the whole legal family reads together.
intro.cn: prejudice 是一个拉丁前缀加那个构成 judge 与 judgment 的「判断」名词，因此整个法律词族可以一起读。

latinIntro.en: The judging noun gives judge, judgment, judicial and judicious; the prefix meaning 'before' gives predict, prevent and prepare.
latinIntro.cn: 那个「判断」名词衍生 judge、judgment、judicial 与 judicious；表「在前」的前缀衍生 predict、prevent 与 prepare。

items.example: The prefix fixes the timing that defines the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀固定了定义这个词的时点。

items.example: The base supplies both the legal and the mental side.
items.exampleCN: 基底同时提供法律与心智两面。

items.example: The Latin compound already had both a legal and a general use.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁复合词早已兼有法律与一般用法。

items.example: English kept the legal and the mental senses side by side.
items.exampleCN: 英语让法律义与心智义并排留存。

items.example: The participle form describes the person, not the opinion.
items.exampleCN: 分词形式形容人，而不是那个看法。

items.example: A different suffix produces the sense of causing harm.
items.exampleCN: 换一个后缀就产生「造成损害」的意思。

items.example: The adjective is common in legal and formal writing.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词常见于法律与正式写作。

items.example: The negative form describes a mind without the lean.
items.exampleCN: 否定形式形容不带这种倾斜的头脑。

items.example: The verb names the act that produces the state.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指产生该状态的行为。

definition_zh: 副手；代理人；议员
definition_en: a person second in rank who acts for a leader, or an elected lawmaker in some countries
core_image: 一把椅子略微靠后，坐着的人随时准备在主人起身时接替
scene: 会议开始前，主管的位置还空着，旁边的人把文件翻到同一页。 The deputy took charge while the manager was away.
sceneCN: 这里 deputy 指「副手」（第 1 个义项：位次仅次于领导、可代其行事的人）；句意是经理不在时副手接管了工作。

derivatives.zh: 代理；代表
代表团
代理职务
委派；授权代理

senses.title: Second in command
senses.definition: a person ranked just below a leader and able to act for them
senses.definitionCN: 位次仅次于领导、可以代其行事的人
senses.example: The deputy took charge while the manager was away.
senses.exampleCN: 经理不在时副手接管了工作。
senses.why: A second chair exists so that the first is never empty.
senses.whyCN: 第二把椅子的存在，是为了第一把永不空着。

senses.title: An elected lawmaker
senses.definition: a person elected to a lawmaking body in some countries
senses.definitionCN: 在某些国家被选入立法机构的人
senses.example: The deputies debated the new law for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 议员们就新法律辩论了几个小时。
senses.why: A lawmaker also acts for the people who sent him.
senses.whyCN: 议员同样替把他送去的人行事。

intro.en: Deputy came through French deputé from Latin deputare, to assign or count as belonging to a task.
intro.cn: deputy 经法语 deputé 来自拉丁语 deputare，意为指派或算作某项任务的人。

items.en: Deputare meant to assign or to count as belonging to a task.
items.cn: deputare 意为指派，或算作某项任务的人。

items.en: Deputé named a person sent to act for another.
items.cn: deputé 指被派去替别人行事的人。

items.en: English took deputy for one who acts in another's place.
items.cn: 英语借来 deputy，指代替他人行事的人。

items.en: The word spread to elected members of parliaments.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到了议会里经选举产生的成员。

items.en: Now it also appears in job titles such as deputy manager.
items.cn: 如今它也出现在副经理这类职位名称里。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deput- stem, and the meaning group gives three people who stand in for another.
note.cn: 形近组共用 deput- 词干，近义组则给出三种替别人站位的人。

entries.definition: to give a task or power to another
entries.definitionCN: 把任务或权力交给别人

entries.definition: to act for someone in their absence
entries.definitionCN: 在某人不在时代其行事

entries.definition: a group sent to speak for others
entries.definitionCN: 被派去替他人说话的一组人

entries.definition: a person who helps someone with work
a person or thing used instead of another
entries.definitionCN: 用来替代另一人或物的东西

entries.definitionCN: 被选出来替群体说话的人

normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一张稍稍靠后的椅子开始，落到一个数人头的会场。

normal.en: Deputy and deputize share the idea of being sent.
normal.cn: deputy 与 deputize 都带着被派出去的意思。

normal.en: A deputy speaks with the leader's voice but not the leader's name.
normal.cn: 副手用领导的声音说话，却不用领导的名字。

normal.en: In some parliaments, a deputy is simply a member with a vote.
normal.cn: 在某些议会里，deputy 就是有投票权的成员。

abstract.en: Picture a hand sliding a folder one seat to the left.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把文件夹往左推了一个座位。

abstract.en: Picture two name cards on one desk, one slightly smaller.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌上摆着两张名牌，其中一张略小。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand in a hall full of raised hands.
abstract.cn: 想象满是会举手的大厅里，又举起一只手。

examples.en: The deputy took charge while the manager was away.
examples.cn: 经理不在时副手接管了工作。

examples.en: The deputies debated the new law for hours.
examples.cn: 议员们就新法律辩论了几个小时。

examples.en: She acted as deputy during the long meeting.
examples.cn: 那场漫长的会议期间，她代理了职务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deputy 记成「代替办事的人」：de 有代的意思，put 像「派」，领导不在，被派去代替办事的，就是副手。

root: 来自法语 deputé，源头是拉丁语 deputare（指派、算作某任务的人）。它先指被派去替别人行事的人，十五世纪进入英语；十七世纪又指议会里经选举产生的成员，现代常见于副职头衔。

sensesIntro.en: From the chair just behind the leader to a seat in a parliament.
sensesIntro.cn: 从领导身后那张椅子，到议会里的一个席位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chair set slightly back, its folder already open.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张稍稍靠后的椅子，文件夹已经翻开。

branches.en: The first sense is a rank that waits one step behind.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是站在一步之后的位次。

branches.en: The second sense is a lawmaker who stands for voters.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是替选民站位的立法者。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of speaking for someone else.
branches.cn: 两个义项都带着替别人说话的意思。

branches.en: In an office, the word measures nearness to power.
branches.cn: 在办公室里，这个词衡量的是与权力的距离。

branches.en: In a parliament, it measures a seat won by votes.
branches.cn: 在议会里，它衡量的是一个靠选票赢来的席位。

intro.en: Deputy grows a small family of assigning and standing in, from the verb to the abstract noun.
intro.cn: deputy 长出一小族表示指派与代行的词，从动词一直到抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin deputare, to assign, from putare, to reckon or think.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 deputare（指派），再往上是 putare（估算、认为）。

items.meaning: a person who acts for another
a group sent to speak for others
to assign a task to another
items.example: They deputed the job to her.
items.exampleCN: 他们把这项工作委派给她。
他的代理职务持续了一年。

items.example: The deputy manager called the staff in.
items.exampleCN: 副经理把员工叫了进来。

items.meaning: the second person in a school
items.example: The deputy head opened the gate.

definition_zh: 算术；计算；运算
definition_en: the branch of mathematics that deals with numbers and their basic operations
core_image: 黑板上排着加减乘除的竖式
scene: 老师没有用计算器，只让他们在心里算。 Mental arithmetic is part of the test.
sceneCN: 这里 arithmetic 是「算术」（第 1 个义项：研究数与基本运算的学科）；句意是心算也是考试的一部分。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：算术的
副词：按算术方法地
名词：算术家

senses.title: The study of numbers
senses.definition: the school subject that teaches adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing
senses.definitionCN: 教授加减乘除的学科
senses.example: Mental arithmetic is part of the test.
senses.exampleCN: 心算也是考试的一部分。
senses.why: Greek arithmos meant 'number' and tekhnē meant 'art', so arithmetike was literally the art of numbers.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 arithmos 意为「数」，tekhnē 意为「技艺」，所以 arithmetike 字面上就是「数的技艺」。

senses.title: The act of calculating
senses.definition: the working out of sums with numbers
senses.definitionCN: 用数字把结果算出来的过程
senses.example: The arithmetic behind the budget is simple.
senses.exampleCN: 这份预算背后的计算很简单。
senses.why: The name of the subject extends to the activity itself: what one does in arithmetic is arithmetic.
senses.whyCN: 学科的名称扩展到活动本身：在算术里所做的运算，也叫 arithmetic。

intro.en: Arithmetic is a Greek compound meaning 'the art of number'.
intro.cn: arithmetic 是希腊语复合词，意为「数的技艺」。

items.en: arithmos meant 'number, count'.
items.cn: arithmos 意为「数、计数」。

items.en: tekhnē meant 'art, skill'.
items.cn: tekhnē 意为「技艺、技能」。

items.en: arithmetike tekhnē was the skill of counting.
items.cn: arithmetike tekhnē 即计数的技艺。

items.en: Latin kept the word as the name of a school subject.
items.cn: 拉丁语把它保留为一门学校科目之名。

items.en: English arithmetic named one of the seven liberal arts.
items.cn: 英语 arithmetic 曾是七艺之一。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same Greek stem; the near-meaning group gives broader or narrower number words.
note.cn: 形近组同出一个希腊词干；近义组是范围更大或更窄的数的词。

entries.definition: relating to arithmetic
by arithmetic means
an expert in number
the wider study of number and shape
the working out of a result
reckoning with numbers

normalIntro.en: Arithmetic is the craft of number.
normalIntro.cn: arithmetic 就是关于数的技艺。

normal.en: The th is pronounced as in thick.
normal.cn: 其中的 th 读作 thick 里的音。

normal.en: Mental arithmetic means sums done in the head.
normal.cn: mental arithmetic 指心算。

normal.en: The adjective is arithmetical.
normal.cn: 形容词是 arithmetical。

normal.en: It names a branch, not a single sum.
normal.cn: 它指一门分支，而非某一道算式。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: a-RITH-me-tic.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：a-RITH-me-tic。

abstract.en: See columns of figures on a blackboard.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上成列的数字。

abstract.en: See fingers counting under a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象桌下掰着的手指。

abstract.en: See a plus sign drawn in chalk.
abstract.cn: 想象粉笔画的加号。

examples.en: Mental arithmetic is part of the test.
examples.cn: 心算也是考试的一部分。

examples.en: The arithmetic behind the budget is simple.
examples.cn: 这份预算背后的计算很简单。

examples.en: Children learn arithmetic before algebra.
examples.cn: 孩子们先学算术，再学代数。

dict_mnemonic.text: arithm（数）加 -etic（技艺）：与数打交道的技艺，就是算术。

root: 源自希腊语 arithmetike tekhnē「计数的技艺」，由 arithmos「数」与 tekhnē「技艺」构成，经拉丁语 arithmetica 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The art of number names both a school subject and the summing done inside it.
sensesIntro.cn: 数的技艺既指一门课程，也指课程里所做的运算。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of figures waiting to be added.
core.cn: 核心意象：一列等着相加的数字。

branches.en: basic arithmetic
branches.cn: 基础算术

branches.en: an arithmetic lesson
branches.cn: 算术课

branches.en: do the arithmetic
branches.cn: 算一算

branches.en: the arithmetic of the deal
branches.cn: 这笔交易的计算

branches.en: mental arithmetic
branches.cn: 心算

intro.en: A Greek compound that became the name of a school subject.
intro.cn: 这个希腊语复合词后来成了一门课程的名称。

latinIntro.en: The number root arithmos also appears in logarithm.
latinIntro.cn: 数词根 arithmos 也出现在 logarithm 中。

definition_zh: 通常地；普遍地；一般地
definition_en: usually, or by most people in general
core_image: 街上人人都这么做的那个默认动作
scene: 这种草药常被用来缓解头痛。 Garlic is commonly used in home cooking.
sceneCN: 这里 commonly 指「通常地；普遍地」（第 1 个义项：经常如此）；句意是大蒜在家庭烹饪中被普遍使用。

derivatives.zh: 常见的；共同的
普通；常见
不常见的
司空见惯的

senses.title: Usually
senses.definition: in most cases or in the usual way
senses.definitionCN: 在多数情况下或以惯常方式
senses.example: The office is commonly quiet after six.
senses.exampleCN: 六点以后办公室通常很安静。
senses.why: The adverb tells how often something happens, straight from the adjective common.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词说明某事发生的频率，直接来自形容词 common。

senses.title: By most people
senses.definition: by or among most people in general
senses.definitionCN: 由多数人或在多数人之中
senses.example: This plant is commonly found near rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物在河边很常见。
senses.why: What many people share is also what many people do, so the word covers the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 多数人共有的东西也是多数人会做的事，所以这个词涵盖了人群。

intro.en: Commonly is common plus -ly, the ordinary English ending for adverbs.
intro.cn: commonly 由 common 加 -ly 构成，这是英语副词最常见的词尾。

items.en: Communis meant shared by all.
items.cn: communis 意为众人共有。

items.en: Old French comun described what many share.
items.cn: 古法语 comun 描述许多人共有的东西。

items.en: English common covered shared land and habits.
items.cn: 英语 common 涵盖共有的土地与习惯。

items.en: Commonly appeared as the adverb of usual practice.
items.cn: commonly 作为表示惯常做法的副词出现。

items.en: It now also marks what is generally believed or found.
items.cn: 如今它也表示普遍被认为或普遍存在的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers adverbs with a similar ending, while the meaning group lists other adverbs of frequency.
note.cn: 形近组收的是结尾相近的副词，近义组列出其他表示频率的副词。

entries.definition: in an easy and relaxed way
when compared with something else
in a way that deserves praise
in most cases
by most people or in most cases
often; many times

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a habit everyone follows, then move to what is widely found and widely believed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从人人都有的习惯开始，再走到普遍可见与普遍相信的事。

normal.en: Drop -ly from commonly and the adjective common remains.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ly，剩下的就是形容词 common。

normal.en: Commonly used is the phrase you will meet most often in reading.
normal.cn: commonly used 是阅读中最常遇到的搭配。

normal.en: Commonly known as introduces the everyday name of a thing.
normal.cn: commonly known as 用来引出某物的通俗名称。

normal.en: The adverb softens a claim: commonly, not always.
normal.cn: 这个副词会弱化断言：通常如此，并非总是如此。

normal.en: Commonly and common share one idea: many people, many times.
normal.cn: commonly 与 common 共享一个意思：很多人，很多次。

abstract.en: Picture a bus stop where everyone stands in the same spot.
abstract.cn: 想象一个公交站，所有人都站在同一处。

abstract.en: Picture the same plant growing along every river bank.
abstract.cn: 想象同一种植物长在每条河边。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd nodding at a familiar saying.
abstract.cn: 想象人群对一句熟悉的话点头。

examples.en: Garlic is commonly used in home cooking.
examples.cn: 大蒜在家庭烹饪中被普遍使用。

examples.en: The bird is commonly seen near lakes.
examples.cn: 这种鸟在湖边很常见。

examples.en: It is commonly believed that practice helps memory.
examples.cn: 人们普遍认为练习有助于记忆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 commonly 记成 common（常见的）加 ly：以常见的方式发生，就是通常地、普遍地。

root: 由 common 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，词根上溯拉丁语 communis（共有），本义是众人共有的方式，后指通常与普遍。

sensesIntro.en: From what happens in most cases, to what most people do or believe.
sensesIntro.cn: 从多数情况下会发生，到多数人会做或会相信。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the default action that everyone on the street performs.
core.cn: 核心意象：街上人人都这么做的那个默认动作。

branches.en: The frequency sense is the main modern use.
branches.cn: 频率义是今天的主要用法。

branches.en: The crowd sense explains why the word can mean widely.
branches.cn: 人群义解释了为什么这个词能表示广泛地。

branches.en: What most people do is usually what happens most often.
branches.cn: 多数人做的事，通常也就是最常发生的事。

branches.en: A commonly held view is both frequent and shared.
branches.cn: 普遍持有的观点既常见又为众人共有。

branches.en: Labels like commonly known as keep a claim modest.
branches.cn: 像通常被称为这样的说法，让断言保持谦逊。

intro.en: Commonly is an -ly adverb whose whole family grows from common.
intro.cn: commonly 是带 -ly 的副词，整个家族都从 common 生长出来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin communis, shared, is the distant base of both common and commonly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 communis（共有）是 common 与 commonly 共同的远祖。

items.example: Such errors are common in drafts.
items.exampleCN: 这类错误在草稿里很常见。

items.example: The practice is commoner in villages.
items.exampleCN: 这种做法在乡村更常见。

items.example: It is the commonest name in the class.
items.exampleCN: 这是班里最常见的名字。

items.example: The commonness of the mistake surprised her.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误的普遍程度让她吃惊。
这样的屏幕如今已司空见惯。

items.example: The two sides found common ground.

definition_zh: 反应迅速的；回应积极的；响应灵敏的
definition_en: reacting quickly or positively to something
core_image: 手一碰屏幕，画面立刻亮起变化
scene: 新系统对触摸的反应非常灵敏。 The new system is very responsive to touch.
sceneCN: 这里 responsive 是「响应灵敏的」（第 1 个义项：对刺激反应迅速）；句意：新系统对触摸的反应非常灵敏。

pos.zh: 反应迅速的；回应积极的；响应灵敏的

derivatives.zh: 回答；反应
回答；回应
反应能力；敏感度

senses.title: Reacting quickly
senses.definition: reacting quickly and readily to something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物迅速而乐意地作出反应
senses.example: The staff are friendly and responsive.
senses.exampleCN: 员工友好且反应迅速。
senses.why: The adjective adds -ive to response, so it describes a readiness to answer.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由 response 加 -ive 构成，描述随时准备回应的状态。

senses.title: Reacting well to treatment or needs
senses.titleCN: 反应良好的；回应需求的
senses.definition: showing a good reaction to medicine, care, or a request
senses.definitionCN: 对药物、照护或请求表现出良好反应
senses.example: The tumor was responsive to the new drug.
senses.exampleCN: 这个肿瘤对新药有良好反应。
senses.why: A good answer to treatment is a positive response.
senses.whyCN: 对治疗的良好答复就是积极反应。

senses.title: Reacting to input in technology
senses.definition: designed to change or react according to input or screen size
senses.definitionCN: 设计成能根据输入或屏幕尺寸作出变化的
senses.example: The website has a responsive layout for phones.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网站有针对手机的响应式布局。
senses.why: A system that answers every input is literally responsive.
senses.whyCN: 对每次输入都作出回答的系统，字面上就是 responsive。

intro.en: Responsive is response plus -ive, from Latin respondere, to answer in return.
intro.cn: responsive 是 response 加 -ive，源自拉丁语 respondere（回以答复）。

items.en: Respondere means to answer in return.
items.cn: respondere 意为回以答复。

items.en: Responsum means an answer.
items.cn: responsum 意为回答。

items.en: Response names the answer or reaction.
items.cn: 英语 response 指回答或反应。

items.en: The suffix -ive forms responsive.
items.cn: 词尾 -ive 构成 responsive。

items.en: Modern English adds the technology sense of responsive design.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「响应式设计」的技术义项。

note.en: Responsive is the adjective of response, close to words for quick reaction.
note.cn: responsive 是 response 的形容词，与表示快速反应的词相邻。

entries.definition: an answer or reaction
to answer
one who answers
acting in response to something
willing to receive ideas
quick to notice small changes

normalIntro.en: Responsive is ready to answer: touch it, and it answers at once.
normalIntro.cn: responsive 是随时准备回答：一碰它，它立刻回应。

normal.en: A responsive server answers requests quickly.
normal.cn: responsive 服务器迅速响应请求。

normal.en: Responsive design changes with the screen size.
normal.cn: responsive design 随屏幕尺寸变化。

normal.en: Patients can be responsive to a drug.
normal.cn: 病人可能对药物有良好反应。

normal.en: The noun responsiveness names the ability to react.
normal.cn: 名词 responsiveness 指反应能力。

normal.en: Compare receptive: receptive is about accepting, responsive is about reacting.
normal.cn: 对比 receptive：receptive 侧重接受，responsive 侧重反应。

abstract.en: Picture a screen lighting up the instant a finger touches it.
abstract.cn: 想象手指一碰屏幕就立刻亮起。

abstract.en: Imagine a door opening as soon as someone knocks.
abstract.cn: 想象有人一敲门门就打开。

abstract.en: Think of a plant closing its leaves at a touch.
abstract.cn: 想象植物被触碰就合上叶片。

examples.en: The hotel staff were polite and responsive.
examples.cn: 酒店员工礼貌而反应及时。

examples.en: Her illness proved responsive to treatment.
examples.cn: 她的病对治疗有良好反应。

examples.en: The app uses a responsive layout on tablets.
examples.cn: 这个应用在平板上采用响应式布局。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「response + ive」——随时能「回应」的，就是反应灵敏的；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ spondere（承诺）→ respondere（回以答复）→ response ＋ -ive → responsive，核心义「随时作出回应的」。

sensesIntro.en: Responsive first means quick to react, then reacting well to treatment, and finally reacting to technical input.
sensesIntro.cn: responsive 先指反应迅速，再指对治疗反应良好，最后指对技术输入作出响应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an instant answer to a touch or call.
core.cn: 核心意象：对触碰或呼叫的即时回答。

branches.en: Quick reaction is the core sense.
branches.cn: 迅速反应是核心义项。

branches.en: A good reaction to treatment is the medical sense.
branches.cn: 对治疗的良好反应是医学义项。

branches.en: Reacting to input is the technical sense.
branches.cn: 对输入作出反应是技术义项。

branches.en: Both a help desk and a patient can answer well.
branches.cn: 服务台与病人都能作出良好回应。

branches.en: A responsive screen answers every touch at once.
branches.cn: 响应式屏幕对每次触摸都立即回答。

intro.en: Responsive is a Latin answering word with the English adjective suffix -ive.
intro.cn: responsive 是拉丁语「答复」词加上英语形容词词尾 -ive。

latinIntro.en: Latin respondere means to answer in return, from spondere, to promise.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 respondere 意为回以答复，源于 spondere（承诺）。

items.exampleCN: responsiveness 指迅速反应的能力。

definition_zh: 小旅店；客栈；（旧式）小酒馆
definition_en: a small hotel or pub, especially an old one in the country
core_image: 路边一栋木屋，门口的灯笼亮着，远处旅人正牵马走来
scene: 傍晚的山道上起了雾，马车夫急着找地方过夜。 They stopped at a small inn where the fire was already burning.
sceneCN: 这里 inn 是「小旅店」（第 1 个义项：供旅人住宿的小旅馆）；句意为他们在一家小旅店停下，炉火已经烧了起来。图中可辨识物件：木屋、灯笼、马。

pos.zh: 名词：小旅店；客栈；小酒馆

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 keeper 构成，义为「旅店老板」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「（板球）回合；执政期」
由本词加 yard 构成，义为「客栈后院」

senses.title: A small hotel
senses.definition: a small, usually old, hotel that provides rooms, meals, and drink
senses.definitionCN: 通常较古老的小旅馆，提供房间、饭菜与酒水
senses.example: We spent the night at an inn by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在河边一家小旅店过了夜。
senses.why: Old English inn meant a house or lodging, and it kept the sense of a place you dwell in.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 inn 意为「房屋、住处」，一直保留「可供安身的地方」之意。

senses.title: A pub or tavern
senses.definition: a pub or tavern, especially one that serves food and drink to travellers and locals
senses.definitionCN: 尤指为旅人与本地人提供饮食的酒馆
senses.example: The whole village meets at the inn on Friday nights.
senses.exampleCN: 每周五晚上全村人都在那家酒馆聚会。
senses.why: A lodging house that also pours drinks became the social centre of English villages.
senses.whyCN: 兼卖酒的客店成了英格兰乡村的社交中心。

intro.en: Inn is a native English word, not a Latin borrowing; it simply meant a place inside.
intro.cn: inn 是英语本族词，不是拉丁借词，本义只是「里面的一处地方」。

items.en: The Germanic root inn- meant "in, inside"; Old English inn as a noun was a dwelling or lodging.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根 inn- 意为「在内、里面」；古英语 inn 作名词指住所或住处。

items.en: Inn is recorded in Old English for a house or a room, especially one used for sheltering travellers.
items.cn: inn 在古英语中已有记录，指房屋或房间，尤指供旅人栖身之所。

items.en: By the Middle Ages an inn was a public house where travellers paid for bed and board.
items.cn: 到中世纪，inn 成了供旅人付费住宿与进餐的公共场所。

items.en: The coaching era fixed the word to roadside buildings for stagecoach passengers.
items.cn: 驿站马车时代把这个词固定在为乘客服务的路边建筑上。

items.en: Modern inns are usually small and old, and the word often appears in names rather than descriptions.
items.cn: 现代 inn 大多小而古老，这个词更常出现在店名而非描述中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that look or sound close; the near-meaning group gathers types of lodging and drinking places.
note.cn: 形近组收形音相近的短词；近义组收住宿与饮酒场所。

entries.definition: The preposition of being inside; same old root, different function.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在内」；同源但用法不同。

entries.definition: The person who runs an inn.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「旅店老板」，由本词构成。

entries.definition: A turn at batting, or a period in power.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「击球回合、任期」，由本词派生。

entries.definition: A larger, modern place to stay, usually with many rooms.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「旅馆」，多指规模较大的现代住宿。

entries.definition: A place whose main business is serving drinks.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酒馆」，主业是卖酒。

entries.definition: A small house, or simple accommodation for guests.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小屋、客舍」，住宿较为简单。

normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用本族语「在里面」的词根，以及这个词的搭配。

normal.en: Inn and in share one root: it is the place you go in to for the night.
normal.cn: inn 与 in 同源：就是夜里能进去过夜的地方。

normal.en: An innkeeper keeps an inn, exactly as the compound says.
normal.cn: innkeeper 就是 keep an inn 的人，复合词说得明明白白。

normal.en: Stay at an inn, not in an inn: the verb prefers the article-free phrase.
normal.cn: 说 stay at an inn，而不是 in an inn。

normal.en: A country inn is small, old and by the road.
normal.cn: country inn 小而旧，往往临路而立。

normal.en: Villages used to gather at the inn on Friday nights.
normal.cn: 过去村里人周五夜里都聚在酒馆。

abstract.en: Picture a lit lantern by a door on a dark road: inside is a bed and a fire.
abstract.cn: 想象黑路上门边亮着一盏灯：里面有床和炉火。

abstract.en: An inn is shelter turned into a business, hospitality given a price.
abstract.cn: 旅店是把栖身之所变成生意，给好客标上了价钱。

abstract.en: The word is old enough to make travel feel familiar before it arrives.
abstract.cn: 这个词足够古老，能让旅人在抵达之前就感到熟悉。

examples.en: We found a warm inn at the end of the road.
examples.cn: 我们在路尽头找到一家暖和的旅店。

examples.en: The inn serves dinner until nine.
examples.cn: 这家旅店供晚餐到九点。

examples.en: He grew up in a village inn run by his parents.
examples.cn: 他在父母经营的小旅店里长大。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: a lodging house for travellers, and the pub that grew inside it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：供旅人住宿的客店，以及在客店里生长出来的酒馆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lantern by a door on a dark road promises bed and fire.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑路上门边的一盏灯许下床铺与炉火。

branches.en: THE BED: an inn is first a place to sleep on the way.
branches.cn: 床铺这条线：inn 首先是途中的睡觉之处。

branches.en: THE ROAD: coaching inns served the passengers of stagecoaches.
branches.cn: 道路这条线：coaching inn 服务驿站马车的乘客。

branches.en: THE BAR: the inn also poured drinks for locals.
branches.cn: 吧台这条线：inn 也为本地人供应酒水。

branches.en: THE VILLAGE: the inn became the social centre of the settlement.
branches.cn: 村庄这条线：inn 成了村子的社交中心。

branches.en: THE THREAD: both senses sell shelter, one of the body and one of the evening.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：两个义项都在出售栖身之所，一个供身体，一个供夜晚。

senses.title: Elegant movement
senses.definition: smoothness and ease of movement or manner
senses.definitionCN: 动作或举止的平滑与从容
senses.example: She dances with natural grace.
senses.exampleCN: 她跳舞时带着一种自然的优雅。
senses.why: This is the sense of effortless beauty in motion.
senses.whyCN: 这是动作中毫不费力的美的含义。

senses.title: Undeserved favour
senses.definition: kindness or favour freely given
senses.definitionCN: 无偿给予的善意或恩惠
senses.example: By the grace of God, they survived the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 承蒙天恩，他们从风暴中活了下来。
senses.why: Grace first named a gift freely given, often from a higher power.
senses.whyCN: grace 最初指无偿给予的恩赐，常来自更高的力量。

senses.title: Extra time allowed
senses.definition: extra time given to do something before a penalty
senses.definitionCN: 在受罚前额外给予的完成时间
senses.example: The bank gave them a month's grace.
senses.exampleCN: 银行给了他们一个月的宽限。
senses.why: Favour in time became a legal and financial grace period.
senses.whyCN: 时间上的恩惠变成了法律和金融上的宽限期。

intro.en: Grace came from Latin gratia, favour or thanks.
intro.cn: grace 来自拉丁语 gratia，意为恩惠或感谢。

items.en: Gratia meant favour, thanks, or goodwill.
items.cn: gratia 意为恩惠、感谢或好意。

items.en: Grace named a gift or a pleasing manner.
items.cn: grace 指恩赐或讨人喜欢的举止。

items.en: Grace entered English with both senses.
items.cn: grace 带着这两层含义进入英语。

items.en: It came to describe smooth beauty of movement.
items.cn: 它逐渐用来描述动作的流畅之美。

items.en: It also gave the grace period of a debt.
items.cn: 它还产生了债务的宽限期之意。

note.en: Grace is compared with look-alike words and words for elegance.
note.cn: 把 grace 与形近词以及表示优雅的词作比较。
